clauses.statement: Every model call resolves to one operator-configured OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint declared as a capability. The host owns the credential, the rate limit and the per-call span; the component owns the prompt template and the response schema and observes no material.

clauses.subject: vendor-sdk
clauses.statement: A crate importing a model-vendor SDK raises `ConnectorVendorSdk`, and the gate enforces the absence across the workspace. A provider swap is a URL edit with no conditional branch anywhere in the engine.

clauses.subject: provider-shaped-step
clauses.statement: {{topology.compose.invariant.pillar-inference}} Swapping the driver moves narration quality and moves nothing about rendering.

clauses.subject: data-fence
clauses.statement: No ingested value reaches a model without a boundary declaring it data. Each value sits between marker pairs whose opening marker carries that value's provenance label, preceded by a preamble declaring the blocks data and followed by a closing line re-asserting the caller's rules.

clauses.subject: marker-derivation
clauses.statement: A marker carries a token derived from the fenced content itself, so closing one's own fence requires authoring content containing the digest of a batch containing that content.

clauses.subject: fenced-value-hygiene
clauses.statement: Control characters are stripped from a fenced value, and a value past its declared character cap is truncated and carries a truncation mark into the prompt.

clauses.subject: operator-template
clauses.statement: The operator's own prompt template stays in the system role, unfenced, as the thing the fence subordinates ingested text to. The idempotency hash covers the template alone, and hardening the boundary leaves a dedup key intact.

clauses.subject: default-embedder
clauses.statement: The embedding capability is a port whose default is deterministic and free of I/O: it hashes token term frequencies into an L2-normalized vector. A first run needs no download, no key and no network call.

clauses.subject: model-identifier
clauses.statement: The model identifier travels beside every vector in an `embedding_model` column, so index identity and provenance are recoverable from the rows themselves.

clauses.subject: default-embedder-reach
clauses.statement: The default is a lexical-vector baseline: a paraphrase is orthogonal to it and cross-lingual recall is undefined under it. Semantic reach arrives through the learned in-process model or through operator-supplied vectors passed as a query embedding.

clauses.subject: distribution-form
clauses.statement: A connector resolves in one of four forms: in-tree by name, a project-local artifact path, an HTTPS URL, or an OCI reference.

clauses.subject: remote-unpinned
clauses.statement: A remote artifact carrying no 64-hex content pin raises `ConnectorRemoteUnpinned` at parse, so it fails the validation verb and the gate alike rather than at first load.

clauses.subject: insecure-artifact
clauses.statement: A plain-HTTP artifact reference raises `ConnectorInsecureArtifact` outright.

clauses.subject: digest-mismatch
clauses.statement: The host re-hashes the resolved bytes and raises `ConnectorDigestMismatch` before they reach the engine.

clauses.subject: pin-requirement-switches
clauses.statement: Two switches close the unpinned local load and they compose by disjunction, so neither side weakens the other: a store-wide policy key the operator sets once, and a per-connector flag the author sets in their own manifest.

clauses.subject: local-unpinned
clauses.statement: With either switch set, an unpinned local artifact raises `ConnectorLocalUnpinned` at build and the refusal carries the digest of the bytes it found, so pinning is a paste.

clauses.subject: requirement-without-a-digest
clauses.statement: A manifest declaring the requirement while shipping no pin parses cleanly and refuses at load: the text is well formed, and refusing to load rather than refusing to read is what makes the template posture expressible.

clauses.subject: manifest-posture
clauses.statement: A manifest ships adopted, carrying a digest taken over the guest beside it on the fixed builder platform, or as a template, carrying the requirement plus a placeholder the pin verb writes into. The presence of a digest separates the two; the requirement flag states what the loader does with an unpinned artifact, not which posture the manifest holds.

clauses.subject: posture-undeclared
clauses.statement: A manifest that neither carries a digest nor declares both template markers raises `ConnectorPostureUndeclared` at merge, and a rebuild sweep judges every adopted value.

clauses.subject: digest-host-dependence
clauses.statement: With the toolchain held constant — one compiler commit, one target, one lockfile, one set of paths — a guest source builds to different bytes on an aarch64 host than on an x86_64 one. Build-script and proc-macro units are host-kind and carry the host triple into a metadata hash that reaches symbol names and therefore linker layout. Each host reproduces itself exactly and the two disagree, the instruction stream being identical across them: stripping symbols restores no layout, and no source edit and no compiler flag converges them.

clauses.subject: pin-verb
clauses.statement: `contextful connector pin <manifest>` builds the guest inside a digest-pinned container on one fixed platform, writes the artifact next to the manifest, and writes the digest into the manifest. `--verify` rebuilds and compares without writing, failing on drift.

clauses.subject: host-built-pin
clauses.statement: `--local` builds with the host toolchain for a build-run-edit loop and states plainly that the digest it prints is host-local; writing a pin from a host build raises `ConnectorHostPinRefused`, a host build reading its toolchain off the path.

clauses.subject: path-remap
clauses.statement: Every build applies a path remap over the source root and the package cache, so where a checkout sits on disk is not an input to the digest.

clauses.subject: native-verification
clauses.statement: `--verify --native` checks the host triple, the compiler and the package-manager build against pinned constants, clears every variable and refuses every configuration key that moves the bytes, and only then builds. Its answer is either the container's answer or a diagnostic naming the input that differs, under a distinct exit status so an unable-to-check runner never reads as a wrong committed digest.

clauses.subject: linear-memory
clauses.statement: A connector runs under 256 MiB of linear memory by default, raised per connector to at most 2 GiB.

clauses.subject: call-deadline
clauses.statement: A read call carries a 30 s wall-clock deadline and a discovery call a 60 s one, each armed by epoch interruption at 100 ms granularity.

clauses.subject: session-budget
clauses.statement: A session carries a 1 MiB logging budget, with messages past it dropped and counted in the session audit, and holds at most 8 requests outbound at once.

clauses.subject: bound-outcome
clauses.statement: A connector striking a declared bound returns the transient variant and may be retried; repeated strikes fail the run fast. Every bound decision is recorded on the run record rather than logged alone.

clauses.subject: world-compatibility
clauses.statement: Compatibility is semver over the world. A guest built against one minor loads on any host advertising a compatible minor, and a major bump is what parts them.

clauses.subject: world-drain
clauses.statement: On a major world bump the old world drains: no new run admits against it, in-flight runs complete or suspend on the world they pinned, and the old host world retires after that. A run is never carried across world versions.

clauses.subject: live-reresolution
clauses.statement: Re-resolving or reloading a connector raises `ConnectorHotReload` while a journaled run holds it live; a new version applies to runs admitted after the change.

clauses.subject: built-in-registry
clauses.statement: The names resolving to a compiled-in source form one enumerated list, which callers reasoning about installed connectors read rather than re-listing. A listed name reaches no component path, so it carries no manifest and has no artifact to pin. A feature-gated entry stays listed unconditionally, so a build without that feature answers with a rebuild hint.

clauses.subject: scaffolder
clauses.statement: The scaffolder emits a compliant crate, a manifest with inferred capabilities, and a round-trip test against a recorded fixture, branching on the shape of the input specification: a machine-readable REST description is the primary path, a REST API documented in prose alone needs more iteration, a graph API scaffolds constant documents with every dynamic value bound as a variable, and a database or binary protocol is hand-written native code against an established driver.

clauses.subject: test-kit
clauses.statement: Three test kinds ship with the authoring toolkit: a conformance suite asserting that discovery returns valid schemas, that opening a table yields a finite stream, and that a position round-trips; fixture replay of recorded HTTP interactions; and property tests over position monotonicity and schema invariants.

clauses.subject: dependency-allowlist
clauses.statement: The authoring dependency allowlist carries a linear-time regular-expression engine in place of a backtracking one, and bounded-depth deserialization in place of unbounded recursive parsing of arbitrary input.

clauses.subject: local-store
clauses.statement: The local context store is the destination a pipeline resolves.

clauses.subject: unknown-destination
clauses.statement: Every destination name other than the local store raises `ConnectorUnknownDestination` at assembly, ahead of any row moving.

clauses.subject: no-host-arm
clauses.statement: The destination world is declared with no host arm, so a guest cannot supply a destination the runtime does not resolve.

clauses.subject: synthesized-artifact
clauses.statement: A synthesized artifact is written back through this same destination and becomes queryable corpus. There is no separate sink.

clauses.subject: schema-reconciliation
clauses.statement: {{store.reconcile.workflow.first-sight-creates}}

clauses.subject: irreconcilable-schema
clauses.statement: A schema change the destination cannot reconcile raises `ConnectorSchemaIrreconcilable`.

clauses.subject: durable-write
clauses.statement: A destination durably writes one batch per call, leaving no half-written batch behind.

clauses.subject: commit-visibility
clauses.statement: Commit publishes a run's data for one table, after which a query sees its rows.

clauses.subject: batch-ordinal
clauses.statement: A write may carry the batch's ordinal within its run, which is the join key onto the run's request ledger.

clauses.subject: http-headers
clauses.statement: The generic HTTP source reaches a credentialed vendor API through a headers configuration table whose values are literal text carrying reference placeholders, so the common bearer-prefix shape composes with no code. A placeholder resolves just in time per read, and the manifest, the run journal and the logs carry the reference rather than the value behind it.

clauses.subject: header-spelling
clauses.statement: A bare name and an environment scheme inside a header value raise `ConnectorHeaderSchemeRejected` at parse, as does a malformed placeholder — unclosed, empty or nested.

clauses.subject: body-format
clauses.statement: `format` decides how a body decodes — `json` by default, `jsonl`, `csv`, or a workbook — and one decoder serves the HTTP, file and object sources alike, so one spelling means one thing wherever the document arrived from. Over HTTP the format is explicit and is not inferred from the URL, a path extension predicting nothing about a response body; the two file-shaped sources infer it from the extension.

clauses.subject: format-key-mismatch
clauses.statement: Three key families raise `ConnectorFormatKeyRejected` at build against a non-JSON format: the JSON record path, every pagination shape, and any decode key the chosen format does not read.

clauses.subject: delimited-cell
clauses.statement: A delimited source lands every cell as a string and an empty unquoted field as null, so a dimension file's schema does not depend on its data and an identifier of `07` reads the same across two exports.

clauses.subject: declared-encoding
clauses.statement: A non-UTF-8 delimited body decodes through a declared encoding label and raises `ConnectorEncodingInvalid` where the bytes are not valid under it, rather than landing lossily and leaving a replacement character inside an identifier.

clauses.subject: clock-column-spelling
clauses.statement: A delimited clock column is an RFC 3339 instant or a fixed-width digit stamp; another spelling raises `ConnectorClockColumnRejected`, the watermark comparing text.

clauses.subject: pagination
clauses.statement: A walk declares exactly one of four shapes: a page parameter with a start page, a next-cursor path with a cursor parameter, a next-URL path, or link-header following.

clauses.subject: pagination-ambiguity
clauses.statement: Declaring two pagination shapes raises `ConnectorPaginationAmbiguous`, honoring one of them silently paging the wrong way.

clauses.subject: page-cap
clauses.statement: A hard cap of 1000 requests bounds one walk.

clauses.subject: page-loop
clauses.statement: A vendor handing back a token or a link it already served raises `ConnectorPageLoop` rather than re-landing that page.

clauses.subject: origin-pinning
clauses.statement: A vendor-supplied next link is followed within the configured origin — scheme, host and port — and the origin is judged a second time against the URL a page actually landed on, a redirect moving a request after the link check and a chain ending where it started still having reached a third party. One hop is exempt: a cleartext endpoint landing on TLS at the host and port as written, a vendor forcing TLS being unable to move the request to another party.

clauses.subject: transport-downgrade
clauses.statement: A hop from TLS to cleartext at the same host raises `ConnectorTransportDowngrade`, as does any hop leaving the configured origin; the redirect status surfaces as the response and the read fails.

clauses.subject: table-pattern
clauses.statement: A table pattern binds table-name segments into the request URL, so one pipeline pulls many streams rather than one endpoint. Each table holds its own position, so streams advance independently and adding one disturbs no other's watermark. Every value bound into a request line is percent-encoded, a table name being manifest text that becomes part of a URL.

clauses.subject: table-unmatched
clauses.statement: A table that does not match the declared pattern raises `ConnectorTableUnmatched` ahead of any request, rather than falling back to the unbound URL or skipping the table while every run reports success.

clauses.subject: placeholder-unbound
clauses.statement: A URL naming a placeholder with no pattern to bind it raises `ConnectorPlaceholderUnbound` at build.

clauses.subject: expansion
clauses.statement: An expansion block names the pointer one of two ways and names the column the fetched document lands under: a template whose placeholders bind from the landed row's own scalar columns, nested ones by dotted path and each percent-encoded, or a column already holding a URL, resolved against the configured endpoint when relative and taken as written when absolute.

clauses.subject: pointer-ambiguity
clauses.statement: Declaring both pointer forms raises `ConnectorPointerAmbiguous`, a row's document being reached one way.

clauses.subject: expanded-format
clauses.statement: The fetched document's own format decides how it is read: parsed and landed as a nested column, or landed verbatim in one text column for an index whose details arrive as XML, HTML or delimited text.

clauses.subject: expansion-order
clauses.statement: Expansion runs after the watermark filter, so the rows that land are the rows that are expanded and a rejected row costs no vendor request. Follow-ups are issued one after another, so an unmetered manifest cannot burst a single host at the width of a batch.

clauses.subject: follow-up-failure
clauses.statement: A failed follow-up raises `ConnectorExpansionFailed` for the whole read rather than landing the index row with its target column absent, committing a position past a row whose detail is missing stranding that row on a forward-only path.

clauses.subject: expansion-budget
clauses.statement: One expanding read issues at most 200 requests of follow-up, judged before the first is spent, holds at most 256 MiB of buffered document bytes, and runs at most 600 s. Each budget refuses rather than truncating.

clauses.subject: template-shape
clauses.statement: A pointer template carrying no placeholder, or binding one into the URL's authority, raises `ConnectorTemplateRejected` at build: the first fetches one document once per landed row, and the second lets a response body name a credential's destination, percent-encoding being no defense where a hostname is unreserved characters throughout.

clauses.subject: pointer-column-missing
clauses.statement: A placeholder naming a column the rows do not carry, or carry as an array, raises `ConnectorPointerColumnMissing` on the first row ahead of its request, which columns a row holds being unknown until one arrives.

clauses.subject: target-column-occupied
clauses.statement: A target column the index already carries raises `ConnectorTargetColumnOccupied` ahead of the walk, judged over every landed row, so an index whose hundredth row carries it costs no follow-ups first.

clauses.subject: walk-boundary
clauses.statement: Every source walking an operator-pointed directory draws its boundary the same way: the configured root is the whole of what the walk reaches, dot-entries are skipped, and the traversal is sorted so a run over an unchanged tree reproduces across hosts. A key selecting how a file decodes is not a key bounding what the walk reaches; narrowing which extensions are read as text confines nothing.

clauses.subject: declined-tally
clauses.statement: A directory walk reports what it declined on the run record, tallied by extension, so a collection whose transcripts never landed does not read as a collection that has none.

clauses.subject: document-grain
clauses.statement: A document source lands one row per page or, past a length threshold, one row per heading — never one row per document. With an operator-supplied base URL each row's link carries its own page anchor, giving a citation a target.

clauses.subject: document-identity
clauses.statement: A document identity is a slug plus an ordinal, for an unchunked document as much as for a chunked one, so an identity does not move when a document crosses the threshold and leave an earlier row serving stale text.

clauses.subject: document-unreadable
clauses.statement: An encrypted document, and one carrying no extractable text on any page, raise `ConnectorDocumentUnreadable` permanently, naming the path — never an empty body on every page, which reads downstream as a document the store holds and has nothing to say about.

clauses.subject: frontmatter-shape
clauses.statement: A note's frontmatter is a flat scalar-and-list subset: a nested map, a block scalar, and a key carrying the reserved producer prefix each raise `ConnectorFrontmatterRejected` rather than dropping a column silently or shadowing a producer-set one.

clauses.subject: conversion-required
clauses.statement: A compound-binary office container raises `ConnectorConversionRequired` naming the conversion command, detected by magic bytes as well as by extension so neither misnaming changes the answer.

clauses.subject: document-truncation
clauses.statement: A reader that reaches part of a document and stops raises `ConnectorPartialParse` for the whole rather than landing the pages it managed, a truncated ingest being indistinguishable downstream from a complete one.

clauses.subject: input-unreadable
clauses.statement: Unreadable input is data rather than a fault: the source raises `ConnectorInputUnreadable` permanently, naming the path and the position inside a structured input — page, worksheet, entry. Permanence is terminal against the retry schedule, and the failing unit is that table's read, so five hundred documents holding one unreadable member answer by name from the run record.

clauses.subject: parse-containment
clauses.statement: {{pipeline.land.invariant.parse-boundary}} {{pipeline.land.refusal.parse-boundary}} A compiled-in source's decode sits behind that same boundary.

clauses.subject: office-part-selection
clauses.statement: An office container is read by exact part name — four parts for a workbook, two for a word-processor document — so charts, pivot caches, macros and drawings are absent structurally rather than by a filter, and no external entity is resolved.

clauses.subject: decompression-budget
clauses.statement: A multi-part office read is bounded at 64 MiB of total decompressed bytes, and on the wire the archive bound is the operator's body cap intersected with that figure. Archive size, entry count and decompressed bytes per part are judged against the directory's claim and against what actually arrives.

clauses.subject: worksheet-landing
clauses.statement: Landing one worksheet is bounded at 64 MiB of resolved cell text counted as cells land, and at 1048576 rows, shared-string fan-out turning a small input into an unbounded output that counting distinct strings does not see.

clauses.subject: cell-indexing
clauses.statement: An absent cell omits its key and an empty existing cell lands null. Cells land by their declared column reference rather than by position, since taking the nth element as the nth column shifts every row containing a blank, and a gap between row indices lands nothing rather than filling every unfilled index.

clauses.subject: cell-out-of-range
clauses.statement: A cell past the header's width raises `ConnectorCellOutOfRange`, and the worksheet header inherits the empty-name and repeated-name refusals of the delimited reader verbatim.

clauses.subject: external-reference
clauses.statement: An external-reference declaration, an external-links part, and a relationship marked external each raise `ConnectorExternalReference` permanently: a cached external value is another workbook's data wearing this one's provenance, and following the link reaches a host the manifest never named.

clauses.subject: workbook-cell-typing
clauses.statement: Every workbook cell lands as a string and a date cell lands as its serial number, the styles part being unread and a number-format id being the author's display choice rather than a type. A formula subtree is skipped whole, so no formula is evaluated and the cached value beside it is what lands.

clauses.subject: workbook-incremental
clauses.statement: An incremental position against a workbook raises `ConnectorIncrementalUnsupported`, a variable-width serial number advancing a lexicographic watermark past rows the run never landed. The pairing becomes legal once the styles part lands.

clauses.subject: report-source-nativity
clauses.statement: A source whose vendor enqueues a report job, bakes it and then pages results is compiled-in native code, waiting being a host capability rather than a guest one.

clauses.subject: report-id-commit
clauses.statement: The vendor's run id is committed the instant creation returns it, ahead of the first poll, the job existing on the vendor's side from that moment. Exhausting the polling budget ends the read successfully with the id committed, and the following read resumes that same job. An expired or failed vendor run id is recreated for the same window rather than surfaced as a failure, expiry decided on the vendor's structured codes rather than on an HTTP status.

clauses.subject: page-drain
clauses.statement: Paging drains a fixed number of pages per read, emitting one batch per page each carrying the position after it, so a large report spans several runs and every one of them commits a position.

clauses.subject: page-cursor-missing
clauses.statement: A response announcing that another page exists while naming its cursor in neither the explicit cursor field nor the next link raises `ConnectorPageCursorMissing` as a hard failure, collapsing the two facts making a truncated report indistinguishable from a finished one.

clauses.subject: report-watermark
clauses.statement: Report watermarks are held per partition — account, grain and breakdown — as a versioned map inside one position, so partitions advance independently and adding one later invalidates no other's progress.

clauses.subject: partition-isolation
clauses.statement: A retryable failure on one partition holds that partition at its committed position and leaves the pages other partitions already drained intact, rather than discarding the whole read.

clauses.subject: stream-identity
clauses.statement: A report type and an entity grain are part of a stream's identity rather than parameters of one: each split's dimension values join the identity key and the watermark partition beside account, grain and breakdown, and a metric list is declared narrower rather than filtered after the fact.

clauses.subject: metric-grain
clauses.statement: A metric is admitted at the grain the vendor computes it and raises `ConnectorMetricGrainRejected` at a grain where it is an estimate, rather than landing a number a downstream sum silently ruins.

clauses.subject: restated-window
clauses.statement: A caught-up partition re-opens its lookback window on every run, and the pull window is at least as wide as that lookback. Each row carries a deterministic identity key over partition, entity, date and breakdown values, so a second pull of a restated day emits byte-identical keys the dedup path folds.

clauses.subject: report-event-time
clauses.statement: A report row's event time is injected as an RFC 3339 instant at midnight UTC of the window-start day, and null where the vendor supplied no usable date. That column is what an ordering rule and a seed ceiling evaluate against.

clauses.subject: ordering-column
clauses.statement: Ordering a report stream by the engine-injected ingest stamp raises `ConnectorOrderingColumnRejected`, ordering by write time letting a late seed outrank a live restatement.

clauses.subject: field-drift
clauses.statement: Report rows stay untyped JSON into the batch, so a field a vendor adds or renames becomes a column rather than a failed batch. Throttling is typed from both shapes a vendor uses: a throttle status, and an ordinary error body carrying a throttle code.

clauses.subject: report-auth
clauses.statement: An authentication failure on a report read raises `ConnectorAuthTerminal` and is terminal against the retry schedule, an empty-but-successful batch reading downstream as zero spend.

clauses.subject: image-row
clauses.statement: An image source lands the provenance row: path, content hash, width and height read off the file header, a capture instant from embedded metadata where present, the file modification time, a modality marker, and a null body.

clauses.subject: image-header
clauses.statement: An image header that does not parse raises `ConnectorImageHeaderUnreadable` naming the path, rather than landing a row of zeroes, and no pixel decode happens on the ingest path.

clauses.subject: quotability-marker
clauses.statement: Whatever later fills an image body records in a companion column whether the text is verbatim extraction, which a citation may quote, or a model's reading of a chart or a diagram, which no citation quotes as the document's own words.

clauses.subject: marker-body-pairing
clauses.statement: The quotability marker and the body are null together and non-null together; any other combination raises `ConnectorQuotabilityMismatch`.

clauses.subject: search-config
clauses.statement: The search source takes a driver, a query, a freshness window in days and a result ceiling, yielding one row per result carrying `url`, `title`, `snippet`, `published_at`, `score`, `provider`, `query` and `fetched_at`. Its cursor kind is snapshot-id, a full refresh each run, and a declared primary key over the result URL collapses a URL that resurfaces across runs into one row.

clauses.subject: provider-origin
clauses.statement: Each search provider's host is pinned at the call site rather than read from configuration: a non-TLS transport and any host other than that provider's raise `ConnectorProviderOriginRejected`, loopback excepted so a fixture is pointable. Adding a provider is a match arm plus an allowlist entry rather than a new pipeline shape.

clauses.subject: search-degradation
clauses.statement: An absent provider key and a provider 5xx are transient failures yielding zero rows and a zero-row run outcome rather than a crash, and a reader answers from the corpus already landed.

clauses.subject: search-replay
clauses.statement: A search read is journaled, so a replay returns the recorded result set and re-issues no billed query.

clauses.subject: unchanged-skip
clauses.statement: A snapshot source with `skip_unchanged` records the input's content digest in its position as a `sha256` and a row count. A matching digest returns zero batches: zero rows land, the position is preserved, and the run records a zero-row success as the skip signal. The option defaults off. {{run.advance.invariant.digest-scope}}

clauses.subject: poll-only-increments
clauses.statement: Incremental loading is cron-poll. A forever-open replication socket is not a read of this kind, its output being unbounded with no recorded request and response to replay, and a position assumes a mostly-monotonic source.

clauses.subject: credential-plane
clauses.statement: Outbound credential material forms a plane of its own, with its own threat model, its own owner and its own turnover cadence, separate from the plane that admits a caller into a store. One mechanism never serves both.

clauses.subject: plane-crossing
clauses.statement: A key whose use is inbound keeps that use when the outbound backend holds its bytes; storage location never transfers a key between the two planes.

clauses.subject: declaration-binds-a-reference
clauses.statement: A declaration lists the credential names it needs in its capability block and binds each to a `secret://<name>` reference resolved at run time. The file that results is safe to commit and safe to read.

clauses.subject: reference-scheme
clauses.statement: `secret://<name>` carries a stable logical name matching `[a-z0-9-]+`. The resolver maps that name onto a backend location; the reference itself is never a storage path, a file name or a key identifier.

clauses.subject: name-length
clauses.statement: A logical name holds at most 128 chars.

clauses.subject: backend-independence
clauses.statement: Moving a deployment between credential stores re-points the backend and edits no declaration, as the mapping from logical name to storage lives in the adapter.

clauses.subject: value-template
clauses.statement: Where a value embeds a credential rather than being one whole, the declaration carries a template of literal text with `${secret://<name>}` placeholders, so `Bearer ${secret://vendor-token}` composes with no code.

clauses.subject: foreign-placeholder
clauses.statement: `${env://NAME}` inside a template, and a bare `${NAME}`, raise `SecretForeignPlaceholder` at parse, naming the value and the offending span.

clauses.subject: malformed-placeholder
clauses.statement: An unclosed, empty or nested placeholder raises `SecretMalformedTemplate` while the declaration is being read, ahead of any text leaving the process.

clauses.subject: environment-is-a-miss
clauses.statement: Template hydration treats the process-environment provider as a miss and continues down the chain; a name no later provider answers raises `SecretUnresolvedReference` naming the reference. No template author reads arbitrary process environment onto an outbound request.

clauses.subject: environment-opt-in
clauses.statement: `CONTEXTFUL_SECRETS_ALLOW_ENV_TEMPLATES=1` re-admits the environment provider to template hydration and emits one warning per process naming the variable and the access it re-opens.

clauses.subject: whole-value-binding
clauses.statement: `env://NAME` binds a whole credential outside the template grammar, for a value that is a credential and nothing else.

clauses.subject: material-in-a-declaration
clauses.statement: A credential-shaped literal standing where a reference belongs raises `SecretMaterialInDeclaration` at validation, naming the key.

clauses.subject: lease-has-no-scheme
clauses.statement: A leased credential binds as `secret://<name>` like any other. The manifest grammar carries no lease spelling, and moving one credential between stored bytes and a run-time mint is a backend re-point in either direction.

clauses.subject: name-is-the-join
clauses.statement: The logical name is the one join between a declaration, a provider entry, a cache key, a record and a run's provider attribution.

clauses.subject: provider-port
clauses.statement: One port answers a reference with material. Every backend is an adapter behind it, and `CONTEXTFUL_SECRETS_BACKEND` selects which adapters the chain assembles.

clauses.subject: provider-chain
clauses.statement: The assembled order runs: declaration-scoped lease provider, process environment, operating-system keychain, customer-operated manager (a cloud secret store, a self-hosted vault, or a customer-deployed encrypting worker), then a tunnel into the customer trust zone where the orchestrator sees no material.

clauses.subject: first-hit-wins
clauses.statement: Hydration stops at the earliest adapter answering the name, and adapters after it are not consulted for that reference during the run.

clauses.subject: hydration-is-just-in-time
clauses.statement: Material enters the process at the moment a request is being built, per read. Neither the declaration, the run journal nor a log line carries a hydrated value.

clauses.subject: redacting-wrapper
clauses.statement: Every hydrated credential rides a wrapper whose debug and display forms print a fixed sentinel. The bytes are revealed at one point: where the host writes them onto the request.

clauses.subject: literal-template-wraps
clauses.statement: A template of pure literal text hydrates into that same wrapper, so a value's handling never depends on whether the author embedded a reference.

clauses.subject: resolver-per-source
clauses.statement: One resolver is built per source, each with its own cache. Repeat hydrations inside a resolver hit that cache, and concurrent first hydrations of one name collapse under a single-flight gate.

clauses.subject: cache-ttl
clauses.statement: A cache entry lives at most 300 s.

clauses.subject: unresolved-name
clauses.statement: A reference no assembled adapter answers fails the source at preflight where the binding is known statically, and fails the call otherwise, raising `SecretUnresolvedReference`.

clauses.subject: no-ambient-authority
clauses.statement: The credential plane holds no ambient authority. {{connector.declare-capability.invariant.ambient-authority}} Resistance to a confused deputy holds while every path that reaches a vendor goes through mediation.

clauses.subject: decoupling-posture
clauses.statement: Four postures order how far material sits from the engine: inline environment credentials, plaintext at rest at the call site, for development; reference plus just-in-time hydration, plaintext held in the host process; an external manager read through the runtime's own workload identity, where the engine keeps references and no standing credential to the store; and a secretless broker sidecar, where the engine dispatches intent and the sidecar puts the credential on the request inside the customer boundary.

clauses.subject: default-posture
clauses.statement: The external manager read through workload identity is the posture a deployment gets with no further choice. The broker posture serves regulated and high-assurance deployments, and covers every deployment where a hosted control-plane component sits in the request path.

clauses.subject: inline-outside-development
clauses.statement: A profile other than development binding plaintext material at a call site raises `SecretInlineCredential` naming the binding.

clauses.subject: lease-is-the-reversed-manager
clauses.statement: A lease provider is the external-manager posture with the trust direction reversed — the engine asks for a short-lived grant rather than reading a stored one — and occupies no posture of its own.

clauses.subject: forwarding-sidecar
clauses.statement: A sidecar that reads a stored long-lived credential and forwards it outward raises `SecretForwardingBroker` at any distance. A sidecar that mints, exchanges or signs a short-lived scoped credential is a lease provider and stands.

clauses.subject: platform-binding-is-a-broker
clauses.statement: A deployment whose credential store answers on a platform-internal binding alone is a broker deployment, and every broker obligation binds it.

clauses.subject: adapter-is-optional
clauses.statement: Each managed backend is one adapter holding opaque ciphertext. The chain and the postures stand with no particular adapter present, and a deployment running on one manager links none of the others.

clauses.subject: know-how-in-an-adapter
clauses.statement: An adapter exposing a provider-specific exchange, refresh or lifetime entry point raises `SecretProviderKnowHowInBackend` at load.

clauses.subject: scope-declaration
clauses.statement: `CONTEXTFUL_LEASE_SCOPES` lists the logical names that hydrate as run-time leases, each optionally as `name=scope` where the minted scope differs from the name.

clauses.subject: head-of-chain
clauses.statement: For a declared name the lease provider answers and no adapter behind it is reached, whatever the ordinary precedence gives. Falling through on a declared name is not available to it.

clauses.subject: shadowed-name
clauses.statement: An adapter behind the lease provider that also answers a declared name raises `SecretLeaseShadowed` at first hydration, naming the logical name and the adapter that shadowed it.

clauses.subject: undeclared-name-defers
clauses.statement: An undeclared name leaves the lease provider with no outbound request at all, so precedence among the remaining adapters is untouched by the lease posture being on.

clauses.subject: empty-scope-set
clauses.statement: Selecting the lease backend while declaring no scope raises `SecretLeaseScopesEmpty` as a configuration fault at startup.

clauses.subject: lease
clauses.statement: A lease is credential material plus one expiry, held as a pair for the length of the run.

clauses.subject: malformed-lease
clauses.statement: A lease carrying no declared expiry, and one whose expiry has passed on arrival, raise `SecretMalformedLease` and count as transient.

clauses.subject: cache-window
clauses.statement: A leased name's cache entry is bounded by the tighter of {{secret.resolve.limit.cache-ttl}} and the lease's own expiry.

clauses.subject: retirement-margin
clauses.statement: An entry retires 10 percent of its window ahead of nominal expiry, that margin capped at 30 s, so a request sent near the boundary still reaches the vendor inside the grant.

clauses.subject: endpoint
clauses.statement: The provider answers `POST <provider-url>/leases` carrying a bearer mint credential, with body `{ "scope": "<lease scope>" }`.

clauses.subject: response
clauses.statement: A success carries `value` plus one expiry field — `expires_in` in seconds, `expires_at` as epoch seconds, or an RFC 3339 instant — at the top level or under a `lease` object. The relative form needs no clock agreement between provider and engine.

clauses.subject: unknown-scope
clauses.statement: A `404` raises `SecretLeaseScopeUnknown` and fails closed as a configuration fault; a declared name reaching a stored credential by fall-through is not among the outcomes.

clauses.subject: mint-rejected
clauses.statement: A `401` or `403` raises `SecretMintRejected`, classed `auth_expired`, with no retry attempted.

clauses.subject: rate-limited
clauses.statement: A `429` carries its `Retry-After` value into the engine's run-level retry, classed `rate_limited`.

clauses.subject: request-rejected
clauses.statement: Any other `4xx` raises `SecretLeaseRequestRejected` as a permanent configuration fault.

clauses.subject: transient-class
clauses.statement: A `5xx` answer and a transport error are transient, and the engine's retry schedule governs what happens next.

clauses.subject: retry-attempts
clauses.statement: `CONTEXTFUL_LEASE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` bounds mint retries at 3 attempts by default.

clauses.subject: retry-backoff
clauses.statement: Backoff grows exponentially from `CONTEXTFUL_LEASE_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS`, 250 ms by default, to a ceiling of 30 s, and covers the transient class alone.

clauses.subject: vendor-requests-on-failure
clauses.statement: A run holding an expired cached lease whose provider is unreachable issues 0 requests at the vendor; the failure surfaces at the provider hop.

clauses.subject: bootstrap-credential
clauses.statement: The engine authenticates to the mint endpoint with one standing credential, itself a `secret://` reference, scoped to minting and granting no vendor access. That credential is the deployment's whole standing surface, and revoking it severs every leased source at the next expiry.

clauses.subject: bootstrap-non-recursion
clauses.statement: The lease provider holds a handle to the chain as assembled before it joined, so the mint reference hydrates through adapters behind it by construction rather than by convention.

clauses.subject: bootstrap-unserved
clauses.statement: A bootstrap name no adapter behind the lease provider answers raises `SecretBootstrapUnresolved`, naming the reference, rather than falling through as an ordinary miss.

clauses.subject: bootstrap-declared-leased
clauses.statement: Listing the bootstrap name among the leased scopes raises `SecretBootstrapLeased` at startup.

clauses.subject: bootstrap-backend
clauses.statement: `CONTEXTFUL_LEASE_BOOTSTRAP_BACKEND` composes a customer-operated manager behind the lease provider, so the mint reference needs neither an environment variable nor a keychain entry.

clauses.subject: calls-per-resolver
clauses.statement: A resolver is bounded at 1 calls against the mint endpoint per declared name per lease window, so a deployment sizes that endpoint at sources-binding-the-name × ⌈run duration ÷ lease window⌉.

clauses.subject: transport
clauses.statement: The mint endpoint is reached over TLS or loopback.

clauses.subject: redirect
clauses.statement: The mint client follows no redirect; a `3xx` answer raises `SecretLeaseRedirect` and the mint credential is not replayed at the named target.

clauses.subject: proxy-ignored
clauses.statement: The mint client ignores any system proxy configuration.

clauses.subject: residency
clauses.statement: Leased material lives in memory for the run, is evicted at expiry, and enters no file, no journal entry and no audit record.

clauses.subject: host-mediation
clauses.statement: The host implements the outbound HTTP interface itself. Every request is checked against the declaration ahead of any socket work, and the host writes the bound credential onto a permitted request.

clauses.subject: no-material-to-a-guest
clauses.statement: No host import hands credential bytes to guest code; a guest names the request and receives a response.

clauses.subject: unpermitted-request
clauses.statement: A request whose destination the declaration does not cover raises `SecretUnpermittedRequest` and fails the guest call loudly, surfacing even where guest code discards the error.

clauses.subject: bound-host
clauses.statement: A source binding any credential carries one non-wildcard host, checked when the declaration is validated and again when the session opens; a wildcard entry alongside a bound credential raises `SecretWildcardHost`. A source binding no credential keeps wildcard entries.

clauses.subject: default-attachment
clauses.statement: With no further declaration the host writes `Authorization: Bearer <value>` using the single bound credential.

clauses.subject: attach-block
clauses.statement: An `[attach]` block maps a header name to a value template in the reference grammar. The host hydrates it and writes it onto the permitted request, overriding whatever the guest supplied for that header name.

clauses.subject: literal-attach-value
clauses.statement: An attach value embedding no reference raises `SecretLiteralAttachValue`; a constant header belongs in the guest's own request construction.

clauses.subject: redirect-pinning
clauses.statement: Every source, credential-bearing or not, follows a hop whose next URL keeps the configured host and port on the same transport or a stronger one. A move from cleartext to TLS at that same host and port is followed.

clauses.subject: weakened-hop
clauses.statement: A hop from a TLS base to a cleartext URL, and a hop naming any other host or port, raise `SecretRedirectOffOrigin`: the redirect status becomes the response and the read fails.

clauses.subject: landed-origin
clauses.statement: The origin answering the request whose body lands equals the configured host and port, so a column's contents and the address an operator declared cannot come apart.

clauses.subject: referer-off
clauses.statement: `Referer` is off on every outbound client, keeping a previous URL and its query string off a followed hop.

clauses.subject: header-presence-selects-the-client
clauses.statement: Declaring any header selects the hardened client and bypasses the system proxy; a source declaring none keeps the proxy. The test reads header presence rather than the spelling of a value, covering a token pasted inline as well as a hydrated one.

clauses.subject: cleartext-endpoint
clauses.statement: A header whose value hydrates from a reference is marked sensitive and raises `SecretCleartextEndpoint` against a cleartext endpoint, with loopback exempt in its IPv4 and IPv6 forms.

clauses.subject: sensitive-header-record
clauses.statement: A run records which header names carried a credential, by name and never by value.

clauses.subject: url-scrubbing
clauses.statement: A URL reaching an error message, a log line or a landed column carries scheme, host, port and path. Query, fragment and userinfo are dropped, each being a place an endpoint carries its authorization.

clauses.subject: typed-url-edit
clauses.statement: Metered vendor traffic and control-plane traffic each dispatch through one client whose error mapping clears the URL as a typed edit ahead of rendering. A URL arriving by another route is scrubbed as text under the same rule.

clauses.subject: credential-in-a-url
clauses.statement: A configured endpoint carrying userinfo raises `SecretCredentialInUrl` at validation, naming the source.

clauses.subject: scrubbed-pages-read-alike
clauses.statement: Two failures at different pages of one walk render identically from a scrubbed URL; the run record's page fields carry the distinction a reader needs.

clauses.subject: mediation-covers-every-egress
clauses.statement: Every path that reaches a vendor — a built-in source, a guest connector, a limiter call, an exec step — attaches through the mediated path, so no second attachment point exists to reason about.

clauses.subject: division-of-labor
clauses.statement: The host drives the OAuth loop from the connector's declared auth policy and writes the resulting token into the customer's manager as a blind versioned put. The manager learns neither the provider nor the lifetime.

clauses.subject: store-holds-storage-and-trigger
clauses.statement: A credential store contributes versioned storage plus a trigger; the function that performs an exchange is connector code.

clauses.subject: expiry-hint
clauses.statement: The host may place an opaque `expires_at` hint beside the ciphertext for cache invalidation — a number the host supplied, not a lifetime the store read.

clauses.subject: static-key
clauses.statement: A static key in a customer manager turns over with no engine step: each run hydrates the current version behind {{secret.resolve.limit.cache-ttl}}, and a version written by an operator is picked up at the next miss.

clauses.subject: oauth-credential
clauses.statement: An OAuth credential refreshes ahead of its declared expiry rather than waiting for a rejected vendor call, writes the new version back into the customer's manager, and clears that name's cache entry in the same step.

clauses.subject: operator-entered
clauses.statement: A development or keychain secret is re-entered by an operator, who updates what the reference points at rather than editing a value the engine holds.

clauses.subject: leased-credential
clauses.statement: A leased credential re-mints ahead of its window with no write-back anywhere, and a re-mint that fails leaves the source with no credential rather than an older one.

clauses.subject: write-back-denied
clauses.statement: A manager refusing the versioned put raises `SecretRotationWriteDenied`, and the run fails closed rather than continuing on the superseded version.

clauses.subject: backend-stores-bytes
clauses.statement: A credential backend holds opaque versioned ciphertext under a logical name and nothing else.

clauses.subject: connector-owns-meaning
clauses.statement: Token lifetime and exchange rules, the refresh endpoint and its scopes, expired-token error codes, rate-limit headers, in-flight caps, retry policy, pagination and cursor kind live in the connector's `[auth]`, `[rate_limit]` and `[retry]` blocks and its code, pinned by connector id and version.

clauses.subject: vendor-change-is-a-version-bump
clauses.statement: A vendor changing a lifetime, an error code or a rate-limit header is answered by a connector version bump; no credential-store redeploy is involved.

clauses.subject: no-master-key
clauses.statement: The engine holds references, and no single encryption key exists whose theft together with a database copy yields every credential. What a deployment protects instead is its own store's key material, inside its own account.

clauses.subject: turnover-preserves-the-name
clauses.statement: Every mechanism leaves the logical name unchanged, so a rotation touches no declaration and invalidates no pinned connector artifact.

clauses.subject: operator-record
clauses.statement: An operator record is the encrypted entry for one logical name plus a plaintext comment above it. The value is ciphertext; the comment is readable in the committed file.

clauses.subject: grants-are-written
clauses.statement: The comment states the exact permission grants the credential carries, in the provider's own vocabulary, one grant per named resource class.

clauses.subject: scope-is-written
clauses.statement: The comment names the account, zone, project or tenancy the credential is scoped to, so a reader resolves which tenancy a name addresses without opening a console.

clauses.subject: creation-date
clauses.statement: The comment carries the credential's creation date.

clauses.subject: expiry-is-written
clauses.statement: The comment carries the credential's expiry, and an absent expiry is written as such rather than left off.

clauses.subject: rotation-location
clauses.statement: The comment names where the credential is minted and rotated, as a provider console path or a command.

clauses.subject: undocumented-entry
clauses.statement: An entry holding a value with no record above it raises `SecretUndocumentedEntry`, naming the logical name and the file.

clauses.subject: unverified-scope-is-marked
clauses.statement: Grants an operator has not established are recorded as unknown, and an unknown marking is a state the record carries rather than an omission.

clauses.subject: record-is-not-material
clauses.statement: A record holds no fragment of the value it describes, so it commits, diffs and reviews as ordinary text.

clauses.subject: rotation-updates-the-record
clauses.statement: A rotation rewrites the creation date and the expiry in the same commit that lands the new ciphertext.

clauses.subject: inventory
clauses.statement: `contextful secrets list` prints, per logical name: the adapter that answers it, the covered scope, the expiry and the days remaining. It reads records and reaches no value.

clauses.subject: expiry-warning
clauses.statement: The inventory marks an entry whose expiry falls within 30 d.

clauses.subject: provider-attribution
clauses.statement: A run's audit records which adapter answered each reference, by logical name and adapter, so an operator reads which posture actually served a source.

clauses.subject: attribution-is-not-policy
clauses.statement: Provider attribution states what answered, not whether the answer was permitted; a re-opened environment path and an ordinary one read alike in the audit, which is what the opt-in warning names at startup.

clauses.subject: material-never-enters-a-record
clauses.statement: The run journal, the run audit and the run record carry references, adapter names and header names. A hydrated value enters none of them.

clauses.subject: derive-source
clauses.statement: `derive` is a built-in source whose input is the context store rather than the outside world. A `[[pipeline]]` sets `[pipeline.source] connector = "derive"`, points it at a landed table, and lands its output through the ordinary write path.

clauses.subject: source-config
clauses.statement: `[pipeline.source.config]` carries `task`, `engine`, `source_table`, `media_column`, `parent_id_column`, `url_column`, `select`, `require_absent`, `media_is_image`, `max_rows_per_run`, `max_seconds_per_run` and `max_attempts`.

clauses.subject: required-key
clauses.statement: `engine`, `source_table`, `media_column` and `parent_id_column` are present and non-empty; an absent or blank one raises `DeriveConfigKeyMissing` naming the key and the pipeline.

clauses.subject: build-context
clauses.statement: A source built with no store root, or with no identifier for the pipeline it belongs to, raises `DeriveNoStoreRoot` naming which of the two is absent. An empty answer in that position reads identically to an archive with nothing outstanding.

clauses.subject: outstanding-set
clauses.statement: A parent row is a unit when it lacks its derived output at the instant of the scan. The cursor is snapshot-shaped and carries no position, so each tick recomputes the list from what the store holds then.

clauses.subject: anti-join
clauses.statement: The source reads the table it writes and drops every parent it already holds a row for, marker rows included. A table that has never been created reads as zero derived parents rather than an error.

clauses.subject: foreign-output-table
clauses.statement: The pipeline identifier the anti-join resolves comes from the build alone; a `[source.config]` key naming another pipeline's output raises `DeriveForeignOutputTable`. One pipeline never marks another's work done.

clauses.subject: cap-after-the-anti-join
clauses.statement: `max_rows_per_run` truncates the outstanding list after the anti-join has removed the derived parents, and never the scanned list before it.

clauses.subject: rows-per-run
clauses.statement: `max_rows_per_run` bounds one run at 25 rows by default. A value of zero or below takes the default rather than lifting the bound.

clauses.subject: attempts-per-unit
clauses.statement: `max_attempts` allows 3 attempts per unit by default; a non-positive spelling resolves to that same figure.

clauses.subject: seconds-per-run
clauses.statement: `max_seconds_per_run` bounds the serial unit loop at 300 s by default for a task that opens sockets, and carries no default for `transcribe`.

clauses.subject: select-predicate
clauses.statement: `select` is a table of column name to value, applied as string equality against the parent row. Every entry matches for a row to be eligible.

clauses.subject: require-absent
clauses.statement: `require_absent` names columns that are null, missing or whitespace on an eligible row. A landed empty string reads as absence, matching a connector that wrote no column at all.

clauses.subject: incomplete-unit
clauses.statement: A parent row whose `parent_id_column` or `media_column` holds null, nothing, or whitespace raises `DeriveUnitIncomplete`; the row is skipped, counted, and the count reaches the run record.

clauses.subject: time-budget-stop
clauses.statement: Wall-clock exhaustion stops the run mid-list, reports attempted-against-total on the run record, and emits the batches already produced. The next tick finds the remainder outstanding.

clauses.subject: journaled-pull
clauses.statement: `derive` sits on the pull-journaling opt-out list; a derive pipeline configured to journal its pulls raises `DeriveJournaledPull`. A crash between an engine call and the commit re-pays for the units of that run.

clauses.subject: unmetered-grant
clauses.statement: Whether a derive pipeline reaches vendors is read off `task` in the source specification, with no connector build consulted. A `transcribe` pipeline declaring a shared-quota grant raises `DeriveUnmeteredGrant`.

clauses.subject: metered-client
clauses.statement: A `link_preview` pipeline opening a socket outside the mediated client raises `DeriveMeteredClient`; every request it makes enters the run's request ledger.

clauses.subject: egress-claim
clauses.statement: A `transcribe` pipeline states on the run record that it reaches its engine in-process or through an operator-declared subprocess. A preprocess step that fetches reports that traffic as the step's own.

clauses.subject: in-memory-scan
clauses.statement: The scan reads the newest committed snapshot plus every uncommitted run file and de-duplicates newest-wins per key in memory, with no query engine behind it. Membership, rather than projection, is the whole question.

clauses.subject: work-record
clauses.statement: The work record carries the scanned row count, the already-derived count, the skipped-incomplete count, and the outstanding list after truncation.

clauses.subject: spine-is-inherited
clauses.statement: A derive pipeline holds the lease, the write guard, the redaction rules, schema reconcile, per-batch durability, the atomic commit, the cursor saved after durability, the run record and the run audit as the write path defines them. The tier re-implements none of them.

clauses.subject: two-sided-binding
clauses.statement: A `[[pipeline]]` names an engine in `[pipeline.source.config]`. A `[derive.<name>]` block at the top level of the machine's own `contextful.toml` states what that name runs. A manifest arriving from elsewhere requests an engine and introduces no command.

clauses.subject: unbound-engine
clauses.statement: A pipeline naming an engine with no matching `[derive.<name>]` block raises `DeriveEngineUnbound`, naming the pipeline, the engine, the file to edit and every engine the machine has bound.

clauses.subject: command-in-a-manifest
clauses.statement: A `command`, `preprocess`, `env` or `allow_hosts` key written inside `[pipeline.source.config]` raises `DeriveCommandInManifest`. The request side of the split carries a name and its bounds, nothing executable.

clauses.subject: task-vocabulary
clauses.statement: `task` is `transcribe`, which turns recorded speech into timed passages, or `link_preview`, which turns the address a landed row points at into that document's head facts and the picture candidates it advertises. An absent `task` reads as `transcribe`.

clauses.subject: unknown-task
clauses.statement: A `task` value outside the pair raises `DeriveUnknownTask` and prints both supported spellings.

clauses.subject: driver-mismatch
clauses.statement: `driver` is `exec`, `fetch` or `"none"`. `exec` and `"none"` stand behind `transcribe`; `fetch` stands behind `link_preview`. Any other pairing raises `DeriveDriverMismatch` naming the task and the driver together.

clauses.subject: inert-driver
clauses.statement: `driver = "none"` binds an engine that lands zero rows and one loud run-audit line naming the key to fill in. It exercises the scan against stored data with nothing at stake.

clauses.subject: deriver-port
clauses.statement: Every engine implements `Deriver`, which owes four things: `engine_id`, `endpoint_host`, `locality` and `run_audit`.

clauses.subject: engine-id-identity
clauses.statement: `engine_id` holds steady across two runs of an unchanged engine and differs across two runs whose parts differ. Two rows carrying one value came out of the same thing.

clauses.subject: endpoint-host-is-bare
clauses.statement: `endpoint_host` is a host and nothing more; a value carrying a path, a query string, a port or a scheme raises `DeriveEndpointHostNotBare`. A path holds tenant identifiers and a query holds tokens, and this value lands in a column many readers reach.

clauses.subject: run-audit-drains
clauses.statement: `run_audit` empties once per pull rather than accumulating across pulls. The tier folds the drained lines into the run record so one run reads as one account.

clauses.subject: anchor-traits
clauses.statement: `Transcriber` adds `capabilities()` and `transcribe(media, opts)`. `LinkReader` adds `capabilities()`, `read_link(target)` and `unmetered_egress()`. A timed interval and a document head share no operation that sorts, merges, dedupes or renders one citation across both.

clauses.subject: asr-capabilities
clauses.statement: `AsrCapabilities` carries `accepts_remote_url`, `max_upload_bytes`, `max_media_secs`, `max_processing_secs`, `cue_timestamps`, `diarization`, `language_detection` and `requires_pcm16_wav`. The caller reads the probe once per run and branches on it.

clauses.subject: timestamps-are-not-synthesized
clauses.statement: An engine answering `cue_timestamps = false` has no interval interpolated on its behalf. A fabricated interval is a citation pointing at a moment nobody observed.

clauses.subject: media-ref
clauses.statement: `MediaRef` is `LocalPath`, a file a subprocess opens with no bytes entering the engine's address space; `Bytes`, an upload; or `Url`, which the engine dereferences itself.

clauses.subject: url-handover-is-opted-into
clauses.statement: A `Url` reaches an engine when the adapter declares `accepts_remote_url` and the operator opted in. An enclosure address routinely carries a subscriber token in its query string, and handing it over places that token in a third party's request log.

clauses.subject: remote-url-unsupported
clauses.statement: A unit whose media is an `http` or `https` address, handed to an engine that declines remote addresses, raises `DeriveRemoteUrlUnsupported`, naming the engine and the `when = "media_is_url"` preprocess step that resolves it.

clauses.subject: media-unreadable
clauses.statement: A media value that is neither an address nor a readable file on this machine raises `DeriveMediaUnreadable` and fails that unit alone.

clauses.subject: transcript
clauses.statement: `Transcript` holds `text`, `cues` non-decreasing in `start_s`, `source`, `no_content_reason`, `detected_language` and `media_duration_s`. An empty `cues` list reports absent timing rather than absent speech; `no_content_reason` is the field that separates the two.

clauses.subject: cue
clauses.statement: A `Cue` is `start_s`, `end_s`, `text`, an optional `speaker` and an optional `confidence`. `speaker` is an opaque vendor label indexing this one recording and identifying no person.

clauses.subject: confidence-out-of-range
clauses.statement: `confidence` is normalized to `0.0..=1.0` at the adapter rather than passed through as a raw model score. A value outside that interval raises `DeriveConfidenceOutOfRange` and the field lands null rather than clamped to a plausible number.

clauses.subject: transcript-source
clauses.statement: `TranscriptSource` is `published` or `asr`, defaults to `asr`, and any other spelling an engine writes parses to `asr`. The engine states the value; the tier reads it and infers nothing.

clauses.subject: derive-error
clauses.statement: `DeriveError` is `Unsupported`, `TooLarge`, `TranscodeRequired`, `Upstream{status, excerpt}`, `RateLimited{retry_after_s}`, `Timeout{elapsed_s}` or `EngineUnavailable`. `RateLimited`, `Timeout`, and `Upstream` carrying a 5xx status are retryable; the remainder settle the unit.

clauses.subject: upstream-excerpt
clauses.statement: `Upstream::excerpt` holds at most 4 KiB and carries no request body. An error string is where credential material most readily travels back out.

clauses.subject: engine-unavailable-scope
clauses.statement: `EngineUnavailable` describes the engine rather than one unit, returns out of the read, and ends the run. Marking hundreds of units failed against one unreachable binary spends every attempt budget in the table.

clauses.subject: link-reader-unavailable
clauses.statement: A `LinkReader` returning `EngineUnavailable` raises `DeriveLinkEngineUnavailable`. Its engine is a different publisher per unit, so one dead name costs one row.

clauses.subject: stub-transcriber
clauses.statement: A stub transcriber ships as a public adapter rather than a test fixture: it answers from a canned transcript with no I/O, derives its declared capabilities from what it can answer with, reports `local:device`, and gives `stub.invalid` as its host rather than a plausible hostname.

clauses.subject: locality
clauses.statement: `Locality` is `OnDevice`, `OnDeviceWithPublicEgress`, `OnPrem` or `PublicCloud`, and each maps to one zone tag.

clauses.subject: locality-is-the-adapters
clauses.statement: The adapter declares its locality and that value lands on every row the engine produces. Where inference physically happened is the one property of a deployment a later reader cannot reconstruct from the store.

clauses.subject: advisory-zone
clauses.statement: The `zone` key in an operator's binding is advisory; a row whose zone column is taken from it raises `DeriveAdvisoryZone`. A config edit relabelling a remote engine as a local one turns placement policy into prose.

clauses.subject: public-egress-fails-closed
clauses.statement: The tag an `OnDeviceWithPublicEgress` adapter writes matches no zone entry until an operator widens the list deliberately. A request line carrying an address a third party wrote leaves the device, and a tag claiming otherwise is false.

clauses.subject: chain-shape
clauses.statement: An `exec` engine is 0 to N media-to-media preprocess steps followed by one media-to-cues engine step.

clauses.subject: step-condition
clauses.statement: A preprocess step's `when` is `always`, the default; `media_is_url`, which fires when the unit's media is an address nothing has fetched yet; or `engine_requires_pcm16_wav`, which fires off the engine step's declared capability. A probed condition leaves no stale transcode behind after an engine swap.

clauses.subject: argv-array
clauses.statement: A step's `command` is an array of arguments and no shell is spawned: no word splitting, no glob expansion, no command substitution. A media address carrying shell metacharacters reaches the tool as one argument.

clauses.subject: shell-string
clauses.statement: A `command` given as a single string rather than an array raises `DeriveShellCommand`.

clauses.subject: placeholder-substitution
clauses.statement: `{input}`, `{input_url}`, `{output}` and `{output_stem}` substitute as whole argument elements. A placeholder embedded inside a longer argument is left untouched.

clauses.subject: output-path-template
clauses.statement: `output_path` is a filesystem-path template rather than an argument element, and is the one place substring substitution happens. The values reaching it are paths the engine invented inside a scratch directory it created, so no unit's data enters the template.

clauses.subject: cleared-environment
clauses.statement: The child receives a cleared environment plus the operator's explicit allowlist and nothing further. A value may be a credential-reference template, resolved through the provider chain and hydrated per unit rather than held on the engine between calls.

clauses.subject: env-name
clauses.statement: An allowlist entry whose name is not ASCII alphanumeric or underscore, or that leads with a digit, raises `DeriveEnvNameInvalid` naming the entry.

clauses.subject: unresolved-reference
clauses.statement: A credential-reference template is parsed at build; one naming no resolvable entry raises `DeriveSecretUnresolved` while the operator is watching rather than at the first scheduled tick.

clauses.subject: chain-deadline
clauses.statement: `timeout_secs` bounds one unit's whole chain at 1800 s by default.

clauses.subject: captured-output
clauses.statement: `max_output_bytes` bounds captured standard output and standard error at 8 MiB per step by default.

clauses.subject: audit-entries
clauses.statement: A chain contributes at most 64 entries of captured step output to the run record.

clauses.subject: step-error-excerpt
clauses.statement: A failing step's error text carries at most 4 KiB of that step's standard error.

clauses.subject: scratch-directory
clauses.statement: Each unit runs inside a scratch working directory created for it and removed after the chain ends, whichever way it ends.

clauses.subject: non-zero-exit
clauses.statement: A step exiting non-zero raises `DeriveStepExit`, naming the step and carrying its bounded error text into the run audit.

clauses.subject: deadline-elapsed
clauses.statement: A chain outrunning its deadline raises `DeriveStepTimeout` naming the step that was running.

clauses.subject: process-group-kill
clauses.statement: The child is spawned leading its own process group and the deadline signal reaches the group. A descendant surviving the kill keeps the resolved environment, holds the scratch directory open past its removal, and goes on spending the machine on a unit already recorded failed.

clauses.subject: reader-enforced-cap
clauses.statement: Bytes past the output bound are counted and discarded rather than buffered, and the step is killed as the count crosses the bound — tested before each wait rather than after an exit. Draining continues past the cap so the child cannot block on a full pipe.

clauses.subject: overflowing-step
clauses.statement: A step whose captured output crosses its bound raises `DeriveOutputCap` naming the step and the byte count observed.

clauses.subject: silent-step
clauses.statement: A preprocess step exiting zero without writing the file its template names raises `DeriveStepProducedNothing` and fails that unit. Continuing hands the next step the previous file and derives from the wrong media.

clauses.subject: stderr-on-success
clauses.statement: Every step's error stream reaches the run record whether the step succeeded or failed. A step that worked while warning about a missing model is the case worth reading.

clauses.subject: command-resolution
clauses.statement: `command[0]` resolves once at build: an explicit path as written, a bare name through the search path. The resolved file is checked for executability, canonicalized to an absolute path, and digested. A search-path change between two units of one run swaps no binary.

clauses.subject: missing-binary
clauses.statement: A `command[0]` that is not an executable file on this machine raises `DeriveBinaryMissing` naming the binary and the step. The operator wrote the command, so an absent binary is a declared intent the machine cannot honour.

clauses.subject: unpinned-path
clauses.statement: A `command[0]` written as a path carries `sha256`; one written as a bare name on the search path does not. An unpinned path raises `DeriveUnpinnedPath` and quotes the digest just computed, so pinning is a paste.

clauses.subject: pinned-file-mismatch
clauses.statement: A pinned file whose bytes differ from its recorded digest raises `DeriveDigestMismatch`, so an edit is re-pinned inside the same reviewable change that makes it.

clauses.subject: engine-id-is-hashed
clauses.statement: `engine_id` reads `exec:<name>@<digest prefix>` over a hash of every step's resolved-binary digest together with the arguments that invoked it, preprocess steps included. A pinned script and an upgraded system tool each surface as a new engine value on the rows after them.

clauses.subject: engine-id-prefix
clauses.statement: The digest prefix inside an `exec` engine identifier is 12 chars of lowercase hexadecimal.

clauses.subject: no-endpoint-host
clauses.statement: An `exec` engine answers with no hostname. Nothing it does opens a socket it can observe, and a preprocess step's traffic belongs to that step.

clauses.subject: blocking-thread
clauses.statement: Credentials resolve asynchronously, then the whole subprocess chain moves onto a blocking thread. Run inline, one process wait holds an async worker for the length of its deadline and stalls every task scheduled behind it.

clauses.subject: blocking-payload-ownership
clauses.statement: The chain's state crosses onto the blocking thread behind a reference-counted handle, and the resolved environment crosses as a plain map that drops with the call.

clauses.subject: output-formats
clauses.statement: `output_format` is `vtt`, `srt` or `contextful-json`. The first two reach the shared cue parser. The third carries structure the caption formats have no field for. Omitting `output_path` reads the engine step's cues from its standard output.

clauses.subject: provenance-sidecar
clauses.statement: An engine step may write a sidecar file beside its cues, named from `{output_stem}`, stating who wrote the words and why content is absent. No sidecar is the common case and leaves the defaults standing.

clauses.subject: malformed-sidecar
clauses.statement: A sidecar that does not parse leaves the defaults standing and says so on the run record. The transcript already produced is kept rather than discarded over a file that carries no passages.

clauses.subject: operator-allowlist
clauses.statement: A fetch engine reaches hosts named in `[derive.<name>].allow_hosts` and no others. The list is required and the party that authors it is the party that owns the machine.

clauses.subject: empty-host-list
clauses.statement: An `allow_hosts` list with no entries raises `DeriveHostListEmpty`.

clauses.subject: wildcard-host
clauses.statement: A bare `*` entry raises `DeriveHostListWildcard`. The matcher strips a leading `*.` before comparing, so a bare star admits a host literally spelled that way and an entry written expecting everything admits nothing.

clauses.subject: malformed-host-entry
clauses.statement: A host entry holding nothing, or one that spells out a scheme, a path or a port, raises `DeriveHostEntryMalformed` naming the entry.

clauses.subject: scheme
clauses.statement: An address whose scheme is neither `http` nor `https` raises `DeriveSchemeUnsupported` before any socket opens.

clauses.subject: address-literal
clauses.statement: A host written as an address literal raises `DeriveAddressLiteral`. A gate that compares names has nothing to compare against a literal.

clauses.subject: loopback-host
clauses.statement: A host resolving to the machine by name raises `DeriveLoopbackHost`.

clauses.subject: host-not-listed
clauses.statement: A host absent from the operator's list raises `DeriveHostNotAllowed` naming the host, and the unit records which name it was pointed at.

clauses.subject: guard-cost
clauses.statement: Each pre-socket refusal settles one unit permanently, costs no request, and leaves the run to continue. One hostile publisher costs one row.

clauses.subject: per-hop-list
clauses.statement: The redirect policy re-applies the host list at every hop and stops rather than follows when a hop leaves it. A stopped redirect surfaces as the response, so the fix is one line of configuration.

clauses.subject: redirect-downgrade
clauses.statement: A redirect from `https` to `http` raises `DeriveRedirectDowngrade` and the chain stops there.

clauses.subject: redirect-chain
clauses.statement: A redirect chain runs to at most 5 hops.

clauses.subject: no-proxy-no-referer
clauses.statement: The client uses no system proxy and sends no referring address. A proxy can move a loopback exemption off this machine, and a referring header hands the previous address's query string to the host being read.

clauses.subject: exec-keys-on-a-fetch-binding
clauses.statement: `env`, `preprocess`, `engine` and `max_output_bytes` on a fetch binding raise `DeriveFetchBindingKey` naming the key. A fetch carries no credential to any host, which is what lets it name more than one; a silently ignored key leaves an operator believing otherwise.

clauses.subject: document-prefix
clauses.statement: `max_document_bytes` bounds the document prefix the scanner reads at 1 MiB by default, and the remainder is dropped rather than refused.

clauses.subject: probe-prefix
clauses.statement: `max_probe_bytes` bounds one range request against a picture at 64 KiB by default.

clauses.subject: hop-timeout
clauses.statement: `request_timeout_secs` bounds one hop at 20 s by default, and is a separate key from the chain deadline an `exec` engine carries.

clauses.subject: retry-after-default
clauses.statement: A `429` response with no usable `Retry-After` header maps to a rate-limit error carrying 60 s.

clauses.subject: head-scanner
clauses.statement: The scanner reads a document prefix and stops at the closing head element or the first body element, whichever arrives first.

clauses.subject: script-bodies-skipped
clauses.statement: Script and style bodies are skipped whole. An angle bracket inside inline code is not the start of an element.

clauses.subject: attribute-reading
clauses.statement: The scanner reads the property and name attributes in either order, resolves relative addresses against the final address after redirects, decodes the five named character entities plus numeric references, strips control characters, and collapses runs of whitespace.

clauses.subject: picture-fields
clauses.statement: A picture may be declared in `og:image:secure_url`, `og:image:url`, `og:image`, `twitter:image`, `twitter:image:src` or `link[rel=image_src]`. The element that named it lands in `image_field`.

clauses.subject: field-order-is-provenance
clauses.statement: The order of the picture elements is recorded rather than used as a filter: every declaration lands as its own candidate, and one absolute address declared under several elements lands once so a consumer's rubric does not count a duplicate as several votes.

clauses.subject: head-fact-fallbacks
clauses.statement: `title` falls back through `og:title`, `twitter:title` and the document's own title element; `description` through `og:description`, `twitter:description` and the description element; `site_name` through `og:site_name` and `application-name`.

clauses.subject: absent-rather-than-blank
clauses.statement: An optional head fact that resolves to nothing is absent rather than an empty string. A publisher who wrote a blank value and one who wrote no element are the same absence, and no column carries a difference between them.

clauses.subject: declared-charset
