clauses.statement: A character set other than UTF-8 declared in the content type header, or in a charset element inside the scanned prefix, raises `DeriveCharsetUnsupported` naming the declared value.

clauses.subject: invalid-bytes
clauses.statement: A document declaring nothing and failing UTF-8 validation raises `DeriveBytesNotUtf8`. A character split at the byte bound is tolerated, since a truncated read ends mid-character by construction. Lossy decoding lands replacement characters in a title column where they read as a fact about the publication.

clauses.subject: candidate-rows
clauses.statement: A `link_preview` unit lands one row per picture candidate at sequence `0` upward, the document's head facts repeated on each, or one marker. Choosing among candidates belongs to the consumer rendering the card, and that choice reads the losers and their dimensions.

clauses.subject: link-row-columns
clauses.statement: A link row carries the shared envelope plus `link_title`, `link_description`, `link_site_name`, `link_final_url`, `image_url`, `image_field`, `image_width`, `image_height`, `image_bytes`, `image_content_type`, `probe_status` and `probe_error`. The document's own description lands in the body column so the table retrieves like any other text table.

clauses.subject: status-mapping-positive
clauses.statement: A parsed head naming at least one picture lands the successful status. A 2xx head naming a picture in none of the six elements, and a `404` or `410`, land the established-empty status settled: a `404` is a positive answer about the document.

clauses.subject: status-mapping-negative
clauses.statement: A 5xx response, a timeout, a rate limit, a transport failure and a redirect stopped at the host list land failed and retryable. A pre-socket guard refusal, a character-set refusal and any other 4xx land failed and settled.

clauses.subject: no-http-answer-band
clauses.statement: A name-resolution failure, a refused connection and a declined redirect hop report an internal `599` status inside the retryable band. Each has an operator-side fix — a host added to the list, a publisher back on the network — and a settled marker outlives the fix.

clauses.subject: probe-never-fails-the-unit
clauses.statement: A picture probe records its own outcome and leaves the unit's status to the document. A candidate the probe could not reach carries a skipped or failed probe status with its reason, and the head facts land beside it.

clauses.subject: image-host-list
clauses.statement: `allow_image_hosts` is its own key defaulting to `allow_hosts`. A social-card picture commonly lives on a delivery network rather than on the publisher's own name.

clauses.subject: probed-length
clauses.statement: `image_bytes` is the file's own length, read from the range response's total or from a server that ignored the range, rather than the length of the prefix that came back. The prefix length is a fact about the probe.

clauses.subject: dimensions-or-nothing
clauses.statement: Picture dimensions come from a helper that declines to answer when the prefix is too short, rather than landing a zero-by-zero pair that reads as a measurement.

clauses.subject: document-host-on-the-row
clauses.statement: The endpoint host on a link row is the document's own final host after redirects rather than the engine's. A fetch engine reaches a different publisher per unit inside one batch.

clauses.subject: media-is-image
clauses.statement: `media_is_image = true` reads the row's column as a picture address directly: one candidate whose field records the row as its origin, the document hop skipped, and the probe standing as the whole of the work. It is a configuration detail of `link_preview` rather than a third task.

clauses.subject: derived-row
clauses.statement: A transcribe row carries `unit_ref`, the parent's identifier verbatim; `cue_seq`; `unit_status`; `segment_id`; `body`; `start_s`; `end_s`; `url`; `transcript_source`; `derive_engine`; `derive_endpoint_host`; `derive_zone`; `confidence`; `attempts`; `last_error`; `retryable`; and `_modality`.

clauses.subject: marker-row
clauses.statement: A unit that produced nothing lands one row at `cue_seq = -1` carrying `unit_status`, `attempts`, `last_error` and `retryable`, with `body`, `start_s`, `end_s` and `transcript_source` null. A marker asserts nothing about who wrote words it does not hold.

clauses.subject: marker-is-visible-to-the-scan
clauses.statement: The anti-join reads a marker, so a settled unit leaves the outstanding set and a population of undone work is a row count rather than a silence.

clauses.subject: failure-off-the-table
clauses.statement: Per-unit failure state recorded anywhere other than the output table raises `DeriveFailureOffTable`. A run whose every unit failed otherwise emits no batch, re-saves an unchanged cursor, and re-selects the same units each tick without end.

clauses.subject: unit-status
clauses.statement: `unit_status` is `ok`; `empty`, where the engine established there is nothing to derive and said so; `unavailable`, where the engine came back with nothing and did not say why; or `failed`, where the engine returned a typed error.

clauses.subject: unavailable-is-the-default
clauses.statement: An engine answering with nothing and no stated reason lands `unavailable`. A source gating on authorization answers a caller it refuses the way it answers one asking about absent content, so a check, a geographic block, an age gate and a quota all sit in that status rather than asserting the recording is silent.

clauses.subject: unknown-status
clauses.statement: A status value outside the four raises `DeriveUnitStatusUnknown`. The two empty-looking populations stay separately countable, since they are different problems with different fixes.

clauses.subject: discriminator-name
clauses.statement: The status discriminator is `unit_status`; a derive table declaring a column named `kind` raises `DeriveReservedDiscriminator`. That name changes a table's genre for its whole history, and genre filters what the read path returns.

clauses.subject: retryable-is-permanence
clauses.statement: `retryable` is null on a successful row. On a marker, `false` means settled for good and is what the outstanding-set filter reads. A marker carrying no value at all reads as unsettled, so nothing is stranded.

clauses.subject: settled-unit-revived
clauses.statement: A unit whose marker says settled re-entering the outstanding set raises `DeriveSettledUnitRevived`. Raising an operator-facing attempt ceiling revives no security refusal.

clauses.subject: attempts-count-what-happened
clauses.statement: `attempts` is the prior count plus one — what was actually tried — rather than an encoding of permanence.

clauses.subject: empty-attempt-ceiling
clauses.statement: A unit in the established-empty status receives 1 attempts in total. A finding one look establishes is not looked at again.

clauses.subject: ceiling-is-per-status
clauses.statement: The unavailable and failed statuses are bounded by the configured per-unit attempt ceiling; the established-empty status carries its own smaller one. A unit whose content appears after the first look stays recorded settled until its parent row changes.

clauses.subject: markers-fold-on-attempts
clauses.statement: Where a unit holds several markers, the status and permanence pair is taken from the marker with the highest attempt count, since that count rises monotonically per unit while file ordering does not. A tie resolves toward the settled reading, which cannot loop.

clauses.subject: citation-keys
clauses.statement: `start_s` and `end_s` are whole seconds. `segment_id` reads `<unit_ref>#t=<start_s>`. `url` is the parent's own link with the same fragment appended, falling back to the media value where the parent published no link.

clauses.subject: keys-union-rather-than-double
clauses.statement: The citation key is byte-identical to the one a feed source lands for the same moment, so a feed that later publishes its own transcript unions onto those keys rather than doubling every passage.

clauses.subject: link-segment-key
clauses.statement: A link row's `segment_id` reads `<unit_ref>#img=<cue_seq>`, and its modality column reads `link`.

clauses.subject: unredacted-error
clauses.statement: Every non-null write of `last_error` passes address redaction; an unredacted write raises `DeriveUnredactedError`. The units this column reports on are row-supplied addresses, where a pre-signed link carries its authorization in its query string.

clauses.subject: missing-primary-key
clauses.statement: A derive output table declaring no `primary_key` of `["unit_ref", "cue_seq"]` raises `DerivePrimaryKeyMissing`. Without it a re-derived unit accumulates duplicate passages beside the originals.

clauses.subject: one-row-builder
clauses.statement: One builder produces both content rows and marker rows, so a marker cannot quietly acquire a column set of its own.

clauses.subject: provenance-on-every-row
clauses.statement: `derive_engine`, `derive_endpoint_host` and `derive_zone` land on every row the tier writes, marker rows included. A row states what produced it and where.

clauses.subject: one-parser
clauses.statement: Both caption formats reach one parser rather than a copy each.

clauses.subject: cue-grammar
clauses.statement: A document is blocks separated by blank lines, each block carrying one timing line and the text below it. Line endings are normalized once at entry.

clauses.subject: headers-fall-out
clauses.statement: A comment block and a bare sequence number carry no timing line and leave the parser without a special case.

clauses.subject: defects-degrade
clauses.statement: A third party writes the document, so a block whose timing does not parse, whose end precedes its start, or whose text is empty is skipped and counted, and the count returns to the caller, which warns once at the end.

clauses.subject: backward-cue
clauses.statement: A block starting before the block already accepted raises `DeriveCueOutOfOrder` and is dropped. Kept, it collides on the citation key and silently replaces a real passage.

clauses.subject: passage-chars
clauses.statement: A passage stays open while it holds fewer than 600 chars. A paragraph of that length reads as an answer and lands the citation within a few seconds of the sentence that matched.

clauses.subject: passage-span
clauses.statement: A passage stays open while it spans less than 60 s, which is the ceiling on how far a citation sits from the moment it quotes.

clauses.subject: passage-bytes
clauses.statement: One passage's text holds at most 8 KiB.

clauses.subject: passages-per-document
clauses.statement: One document yields at most 2000 rows of passages.

clauses.subject: rolling-overlap
clauses.statement: A rolling caption display restates the line above before appending the next few words. The parser strips the longest whole-word suffix of the previous cue that prefixes the current one.

clauses.subject: overlap-gate
clauses.statement: The strip applies when the overlap covers the whole cue or runs to two words or more, and when the two cues are contiguous. A display rolls within one breath, so two cues a minute apart carrying the same words are a speaker repeating themselves and both copies land.

clauses.subject: single-file-run
clauses.statement: `contextful derive test <engine> --media <file>` builds the named engine, runs it against one file on disk, and prints the parsed transcript together with every step's captured error stream.

clauses.subject: identical-build
clauses.statement: The verb resolves the same binding, the same search path, the same content pins and the same environment allowlist a scheduled pipeline resolves. A cheaper build path proves nothing about the pipeline.

clauses.subject: no-side-effects
clauses.statement: The verb writes nothing and reads no store.

clauses.subject: json-output
clauses.statement: `--json` emits one object carrying the engine identifier, the zone, the cue-timestamp capability, both engine claims, the text and the cues, with no human-readable line above it.

clauses.subject: unsupported-driver
clauses.statement: A `fetch` engine named to the verb raises `DeriveTestEngineUnsupported` with the message a pipeline gives for the same pairing.

clauses.subject: subject-tuple
clauses.statement: A subject is a tuple: the agent, the host it runs on, the principal it acts on behalf of, the task scope, the declared inference zone, and an incognito flag. A credential binds the subset it names. A human, a service account and a timer-fired run use the same tuple with inapplicable members set to a wildcard or omitted.

clauses.subject: tuple-subset
clauses.statement: A credential minted for one combination of agent, principal and task admits under that combination and no other. The grant attaches to the named subset, never to the agent alone.

clauses.subject: attestation-label
clauses.statement: Each member carries an attestation attribute reading verified or self-asserted. Agent, host, task scope and zone are self-asserted and travel labeled as such wherever the tuple is rendered. A self-asserted member is never presented as identity.

clauses.subject: on-behalf-of
clauses.statement: `on_behalf_of` is the verified member, checked at the mint against the issuing identity provider, and it is the key an admission carries forward as the reader's identity. A client acting as its own legitimate user sits inside that user's data; possession binding and a short lifetime are what bound a stolen credential.

clauses.subject: subject-value
clauses.statement: Every subject value is checked at the mint: non-empty, at most 256 B, no control character, and no leading or trailing whitespace.

clauses.subject: padded-value
clauses.statement: The command-line mint trims a padded subject value; the automated exchange refuses one and raises `AuthoritySubjectMalformed`. A value failing any other hygiene rule raises the same identifier on both paths.

clauses.subject: subject-scheme
clauses.statement: A scheme prefix on a subject value is a convention of the deployment's claim template rather than a rule the mint applies. A bare identifier is legal, and every consumer resolves the value exactly as minted.

clauses.subject: normalization
clauses.statement: The verified tuple is normalized once — each value trimmed, each blank member dropped — before any consumer reads it. A subject value is never re-normalized at a point of use, so one padded identity cannot behave as two.

clauses.subject: subjectless-credential
clauses.statement: A credential carrying no subject member at all is refused at admission with `AuthoritySubjectMissing`. The refusal names the surface and echoes no value.

clauses.subject: identity-link
clauses.statement: An identity link maps a source principal onto a subject over fields the identity provider verified, never over display-name similarity or a heuristic match. `method` records how the link was made — `scim_email`, `oidc_sub`, `operator_asserted` — and `confidence` is recorded beside it without relaxing anything.

clauses.subject: link-method
clauses.statement: A link whose method is `operator_asserted` authorizes nothing; it exists for an explanation trace and for staging a mapping. An authorization join consuming such a row raises `AuthorityLinkUnverified`. The two methods that authorize are `scim_email` and `oidc_sub`.

clauses.subject: directory-link
clauses.statement: A source-account-to-subject link is written by directory provisioning out of the identity provider. A value a source's profile interface returns at request time is read as data and not as a link; a profile field is editable by its own holder wherever single sign-on is unenforced.

clauses.subject: unlinked-principal
clauses.statement: A subject whose source principal resolves to no link reads nothing from that source rather than everything. A missing link fails as a denial.

clauses.subject: agent-ceiling
clauses.statement: A sub-agent spawned mid-task holds its parent's reachable set or a subset of it. An agent never out-reads the human it acts for.

clauses.subject: incognito-member
clauses.statement: The incognito flag is a subject member the caller sets and the admitted tuple carries forward unchanged. A derivation turns it on and never off.

clauses.subject: subject-rebinding
clauses.statement: A derivation naming an `on_behalf_of` different from its parent's raises `AuthoritySubjectRebound`. The verified member is not attenuable onto another person.

clauses.subject: delegation-profile
clauses.statement: Delegated authority travels as an attenuable, chain-signed credential read against a versioned profile that names the exact facts, checks and restriction tuples this engine admits. The underlying library owns serialization, signatures, block chaining and evaluation; the profile and its mapping onto authority are owned here.

clauses.subject: unrecognized-element
clauses.statement: A credential carrying a block version, predicate, rule or restriction the profile does not name raises `ProfileElementUnrecognized`. It is never admitted as though it were unconstrained.

clauses.subject: reserved-fact
clauses.statement: Current time, deployment audience, resolved resources and authenticated request identity are reserved facts the engine supplies. A token block introducing a fact into that space raises `ProfileReservedFact`.

clauses.subject: evaluator-bound
clauses.statement: The evaluator runs with no third-party block, no external function, no recursion and no regular-expression predicate, under declared authorizer fact and iteration ceilings. Input past a ceiling raises `ProfileEvaluationBudget` rather than being evaluated to completion.

clauses.subject: appended-block
clauses.statement: A block appended after the first contributes no authority fact to an allow decision. Appending narrows the credential or adds nothing to it.

clauses.subject: unevaluated-restriction
clauses.statement: A grant carrying a row restriction or an aggregate bound for which no read evaluator exists raises `ProfileRestrictionUnevaluated` — at the mint, at derivation on both the parent and the proposed child, and at admission. No verifiable credential carries one.

clauses.subject: wire-field
clauses.statement: A refused restriction field stays declared in the wire shape. Claims parsing skips an unknown key, and a declared field is parsed at every admission, so a credential carrying it stays constrained by it.

clauses.subject: profile-module
clauses.statement: A gateway forwards the credential it received and the engine owns the final data authorization. Where both decide the same question they execute one pinned profile module, compiled natively and to WebAssembly, rather than two hand-written verifiers.

clauses.subject: declared-scope
clauses.statement: Introspection reports the scope a credential declares, legible without running anything, since the profile bounds what a block says. Effective authority is settled afterwards by table policy, source access lists, time bounds and revocation.

clauses.subject: scoped-session
clauses.statement: Authorization yields a scoped session carrying every restriction the credential expressed. A statement touching two tables requires both accesses authorized as one coherent grant; actions and tables never flatten into two independent allowlists.

clauses.subject: profile-version
clauses.statement: A checkpoint reading a profile version it does not implement raises `ProfileVersionUnsupported`. Widening the profile mints a new version rather than relaxing an existing one.

clauses.subject: admission-decides-entry
clauses.statement: Admission decides entry and nothing more, and adopting a credential format creates no obligation to translate that format's language into a query. {{enforcement.compose.invariant.protection-is-a-rewrite}}

clauses.subject: grant
clauses.statement: A grant names actions, table patterns, an optional tenant scope, optional aggregate and disclosure constraints, and an optional query-template allowlist. An absent constraint leaves that dimension unconstrained; an absent allowlist confers no template access.

clauses.subject: action
clauses.statement: The action vocabulary holds four verbs: `read` covers every row-returning surface, `write` lands rows, `execute` fires a run, and `admin` mints.

clauses.subject: unknown-action
clauses.statement: An action token outside the vocabulary raises `GrantActionUnknown`, at the mint and at admission alike.

clauses.subject: granted-pattern
clauses.statement: A granted table pattern takes three forms: a bare star covering every table; a prefix followed by a star, covering the prefix itself and everything beneath it; and any other string, matched exactly. A concrete pattern never covers the star.

clauses.subject: malformed-pattern
clauses.statement: A pattern carrying a star anywhere but its final position raises `GrantPatternMalformed`. One implementation of the three forms serves derivation legality, view registration, tool visibility and replica object selection.

clauses.subject: star-pattern
clauses.statement: The star pattern is an ordinary grant, bounded by the credential's actions, audience and expiry and visible in the audit record. An operator legitimately holding the whole store names it once rather than enumerating tables and silently losing each new one.

clauses.subject: tenant-scope
clauses.statement: A grant scopes below the table onto a table-and-tenant pair, where the tenant is an opaque byte string bound to that table's outermost partition column.

clauses.subject: tenant-identity
clauses.statement: The grant's tenant value, the partition key written on disk and the consumer's own tenant identifier are the same bytes. The mint stamps it verbatim, the build writes the key byte for byte, and comparison is a bound-parameter equality with no collation in the loop. A value differing by trimming, case folding or Unicode normalization is a different tenant and reads nothing.

clauses.subject: unbindable-tenant
clauses.statement: A tenant-scoped grant against a table that declares no bare outermost partition column raises `GrantTenantUnbindable` at admission. A scope with nothing to bind onto does not widen to the whole table.

clauses.subject: tenant-child-lifetime
clauses.statement: A tenant-scoped child credential is derived per query and carries a lifetime of 15 min.

clauses.subject: tenant-child
clauses.statement: A consumer's service holds one broader parent and derives the per-query child locally. A credential carried across a durable run's steps is persisted by that run's own record, and what is read back from it has already lapsed.

clauses.subject: template-allowlist
clauses.statement: A query-template allowlist is a granted capability with the opposite polarity to a restriction: deny by default. An absent list authorizes no template, a star authorizes every template the manifest declares, and a child names only identifiers its parent named or covered.

clauses.subject: template-not-allowed
clauses.statement: Invoking a template outside the allowlist raises `GrantTemplateNotAllowed`, and a template the credential does not cover is absent from the projected tool listing. Guessing an identifier reaches the same refusal.

clauses.subject: pipeline-resource
clauses.statement: A pipeline identifier is a read resource in its own right. Listing it, describing it and tracing its runs each require a read grant covering that identifier, and a grant over the tables a pipeline lands does not confer it.

clauses.subject: ungranted-pipeline
clauses.statement: Describing a pipeline no grant covers raises `GrantPipelineNotCovered` and names it, rather than answering with an empty run history — an empty history is itself a claim that nothing ran. Listing filters down to the covered identifiers and raises the same identifier when the credential covers none, while a project declaring no pipelines answers with an empty list.

clauses.subject: run-trace
clauses.statement: Tracing a run gates on the pipeline resolved from the run record and raises `GrantRunTraceDenied` without echoing which pipeline that was. A held run identifier does not become an oracle for its owner.

clauses.subject: effective-row-ceiling
clauses.statement: The effective row ceiling of a read is the smallest of the grant's ceiling, the request's own, the template's where one is used, and the serving face's. A component declaring no ceiling imposes none.

clauses.subject: aggregate-constraint
clauses.statement: An aggregate grant carries a minimum group size, a maximum single-contributor share of the metric mass, the permitted aggregate functions, a ceiling on groups per query and a row ceiling. A write-only or aggregate-only grant contributes no table to a raw read.

clauses.subject: offline-derivation
clauses.statement: A holder derives a narrower child with no round trip to the issuer. Derivation is a local signature over the parent's transmitted bytes together with the appended block.

clauses.subject: narrowing
clauses.statement: A child's actions, table patterns, tenant scope, aggregate constraints and template allowlist are each no broader than its parent's. The comparison runs when the child is minted and again at admission.

clauses.subject: widening
clauses.statement: A proposed child broader than its parent on any dimension raises `AttenuationWidens` and names the dimension that widened.

clauses.subject: child-validity
clauses.statement: A child's validity window lies inside its parent's. Derivation shortens an expiry and extends none.

clauses.subject: expiry-extension
clauses.statement: A derivation carrying an expiry past its parent's raises `AttenuationExpiryExtended`.

clauses.subject: tenant-drop
clauses.statement: Adding a tenant scope to an unscoped parent narrows and is admitted; repeating the parent's scope unchanged is admitted; dropping the scope or naming another tenant raises `AttenuationTenantDropped`. The first widens the child back to the whole table, the second aims it at data the parent never held.

clauses.subject: chain-proof
clauses.statement: The chain-final proof advances an ephemeral key on each appended block, so a holder of a child lacks the proof the parent prefix verifies under. Truncating a chain back to a broader prefix yields no verifiable credential.

clauses.subject: bearer-delegation
clauses.statement: Derivation proves the chain and not the identity of the new holder. A hop that authenticates its new actor runs through issuer-mediated exchange instead.

clauses.subject: parent-intact
clauses.statement: Derivation appends a block and rewrites nothing in the parent's bytes. The parent stays independently verifiable and independently withdrawable.

clauses.subject: derivation-order
clauses.statement: Derivation composes: a grandchild narrows against the child it came from, and admission re-checks the whole chain rather than its last hop alone.

clauses.subject: local-check
clauses.statement: A deriving holder runs the same narrowing comparison the checkpoint runs, so an illegal child fails inside the deriving process rather than at its first request.

clauses.subject: sub-agent
clauses.statement: An agent fanning work out derives one child per sub-agent, each bound to that sub-agent's own key pair and each no broader than what the agent itself holds.

clauses.subject: issuance-ceiling
clauses.statement: A project persists an issuance policy naming the longest lifetime any mint path produces, at most 24 h, together with the audience stamped on a credential minted without an explicit one. The policy is tracked in version control, so every clone enforces one number.

clauses.subject: lifetime-above-ceiling
clauses.statement: An explicitly requested lifetime above the persisted ceiling raises `IssuanceLifetimeAboveCeiling` and is never quietly shortened. A configuration-derived exchange lifetime is clamped down to the ceiling instead.

clauses.subject: ceiling-lowering
clauses.statement: Lowering the ceiling records the previous value and the instant of the lowering. A grace guard validates against the recorded value until the last credential minted under it can have lapsed; raising the ceiling prints a reminder to re-validate the rotation grace.

clauses.subject: principal-required
clauses.statement: Issuance refuses a grant of write or execute whose subject names no `on_behalf_of`, raising `IssuancePrincipalRequired`. Those two actions are the ones whose exercise lands rows, and a landed row carries that principal. Read-only grants meet no such condition.

clauses.subject: default-action-set
clauses.statement: The default action set of a mint is `read` alone, so an ordinary mint meets no principal condition and names no `on_behalf_of` unless a caller asks for one.

clauses.subject: absent-author
clauses.statement: An absent authorship value means no capability credential authorized that write — the project's own owner presenting nothing, or a run fired by a timer. It never means a credential verified and named no principal, since that shape does not survive the mint.

clauses.subject: authoring-posture
clauses.statement: The authoring posture is an argument every project-load site supplies. A `session` posture verifies one ambient credential and authors every write through that project by its principal. A `per_request` posture withholds the ambient principal entirely, so a write arriving unaccompanied is authored by nobody rather than by the process.

clauses.subject: one-credential
clauses.statement: A served face admits one thing: a verified capability credential. No static perimeter bearer, no shared secret between a gateway and the engine, and no unauthenticated owner path exists, behind a flag or otherwise.

clauses.subject: missing-issuer-key
clauses.statement: A face configured with no issuer key raises `IssuerKeyMissing`, declines to start, and prints the command that fixes it. The process binds no port it serves nothing from.

clauses.subject: unresolvable-key-reference
clauses.statement: A set-but-unresolvable issuer key reference raises `IssuerKeyUnresolvable` rather than falling back onto a fabricated local key.

clauses.subject: signing-port
clauses.statement: Minting runs through a provider-agnostic signing port. A seed file, a resolved secret reference, a cloud key-management service, a hardware security module and a remote signing oracle are adapters behind that one interface, and the minting path is unchanged by which one is bound.

clauses.subject: custody-posture
clauses.statement: Custody has three postures of increasing strength: a seed file on disk; a reference resolved to the seed at mint time; and a signing oracle that returns a signature over bytes the host sends.

clauses.subject: seed-custody
clauses.statement: At the oracle posture the signing seed never crosses the custodian's boundary, and each mint is recorded there as a signing call. Supporting a signature scheme is a separate question from supporting a remote signer.

clauses.subject: algorithm-claim
clauses.statement: A credential carries a signed algorithm claim naming Ed25519, the default, or ECDSA over the P-256 curve. The pinned key's own scheme is authoritative and the claim is cross-checked against it.

clauses.subject: algorithm-mismatch
clauses.statement: A claim naming a scheme other than the pinned key's raises `SignatureAlgorithmMismatch`. No credential selects the scheme that verifies it, and no downgrade is expressible.

clauses.subject: unauthorized-mint
clauses.statement: A mint endpoint requires a grant carrying the `admin` action, optionally behind mutual transport authentication, and raises `IssuanceUnauthorized` otherwise. Issuance authorizes itself with the same primitive as every other action.

clauses.subject: replica-mint
clauses.statement: A replica is provisioned with the issuer's public key and holds no signing material; a mint attempted there raises `ReplicaCannotIssue`. A credential minted by the primary admits at the replica unchanged.

clauses.subject: zone-wildcard
clauses.statement: Issuance refuses a subject declaring a wildcard inference zone, raising `IssuanceZoneWildcard`. A wildcard belongs on the data side of a placement decision.

clauses.subject: mint-scope
clauses.statement: Persisted-ceiling enforcement binds a mint run from inside the project tree. A mint run outside it is governed at the verifying checkpoint by the rotation-grace validation instead.

clauses.subject: key-rotation-cadence
clauses.statement: The signing key that verifies capability credentials rotates every 90 d, and immediately on suspected compromise.

clauses.subject: admitted-authority
clauses.statement: Verification produces an admitted-authority value carrying the normalized subject tuple and the grants it narrows to. Every read surface and every row-landing effect accepts that value as an argument; nothing downstream re-reads the environment, re-parses a credential or consults a task-local. Two callers writing through one daemon carry two authors, and neither carries the daemon's.

clauses.subject: no-fabricating-constructor
clauses.statement: The admitted-authority type exposes no constructor that produces a value without a verification — no default, no assume-admitted escape. The session principal and the enforcement identity are two readings of one admission.

clauses.subject: re-read
clauses.statement: Admission is a moment and authority is re-read at each effect. Expiry, the revocation epoch and the policy version are evaluated against the carried value at the effect about to act, so an execution long enough to straddle a lapse stops at its next effect rather than completing on the state it began under.

clauses.subject: format-trait
clauses.statement: The wire format is reached through one interface carrying four operations: issue, attenuate, verify, introspect. Enforcement reads typed grants and subject values, and no enforcement call site names a credential type.

clauses.subject: envelope
clauses.statement: The wire shape is a version-tagged, dot-delimited detached-signature envelope: a version segment, base64url claims, and the issuer's base64url signature, gaining a base64url attenuation segment and a holder signature once derived.

clauses.subject: signature-coverage
clauses.statement: Each signature covers the segments as transmitted — the issuer signs the first pair, a holder's derivation signs the leading four. A verifier checks over segments it can see rather than over a re-serialization of a parsed structure, so claim field order and an omitted optional field lie outside every signature and adding a claim breaks no foreign verifier.

clauses.subject: bad-signature
clauses.statement: A segment whose signature does not check against a pinned key raises `SignatureInvalid`, and the credential admits nothing.

clauses.subject: audience-mismatch
clauses.statement: A checkpoint declaring an expected audience raises `AudienceMismatch` for a credential whose audience differs and for one carrying no audience at all, so a credential minted for one store is not replayable against another. An undeclared expected audience performs no such check, which is the local development shape.

clauses.subject: timestamp-grammar
clauses.statement: Every checkpoint decodes a credential's timestamps into validated instants under one grammar, and comparison runs on instants rather than on strings.

clauses.subject: malformed-timestamp
clauses.statement: A timestamp that does not decode under that grammar raises `TimestampMalformed`, identically wherever it is read, so a malformed or offset expiry cannot be read one way at a gateway and another way at the engine.

clauses.subject: expired
clauses.statement: A credential whose expiry precedes the evaluation instant raises `AuthorityExpired`, at admission and again at each later effect.

clauses.subject: possession-proof
clauses.statement: Every credential carries a confirmation claim holding the thumbprint of a public key its client possesses. Each request carries a signature over the method, the target, a digest of the body and a nonce, produced with the matching private key.

clauses.subject: possession-proof
clauses.statement: A request whose binding signature does not check against the confirmation thumbprint raises `PossessionProofInvalid`. Holding the credential without its private key admits nothing, and the check makes no claim about what the agent is.

clauses.subject: replayed-nonce
clauses.statement: A request whose binding nonce repeats inside the checkpoint's replay window raises `PossessionProofReplayed`, so a captured request is not re-sendable while its credential is still live.

clauses.subject: public-key-only
clauses.statement: A verifying checkpoint holds public key material and no secret. Compromising one mints no credential and widens none, and admission runs with no call to an issuer or a policy service.

clauses.subject: key-set
clauses.statement: A verifier accepts a set of issuer keys rather than a single key. Comma-separated static pins cover a manual rotation; a project-published key route — unauthenticated, per-key opt-in, returning the current and the non-retired versions — covers a scheduled one.

clauses.subject: key-set-refresh
clauses.statement: A published key set is refreshed on a 300 s lifetime, with one refresh-and-retry on a signature failure, so a rotation is picked up at the first credential minted under the new key. Refreshes are single-flight and a failure-forced refresh is throttled.

clauses.subject: key-set-unavailable
clauses.statement: Opting into a published key set and then failing to obtain one refuses every credential: the engine declines to start and a gateway answers `503`, raising `KeySetUnavailable`. A static pin rescues neither, and a malformed pin answers the same way: the refusal covers every credential a caller presents.

clauses.subject: key-set-staleness
clauses.statement: A fetch failure serves the last-known-good set while its total age, measured from the last successful fetch and inclusive of the refresh interval, stays under 1 h. Past that age the checkpoint raises `KeySetStale`.

clauses.subject: short-lifetime
clauses.statement: A short lifetime is the primary instrument of withdrawal. A credential lapses inside the interval a list of withdrawn identifiers takes to propagate, and ordinary operation keeps no such list in step.

clauses.subject: denylist
clauses.statement: A denylist keyed on the credential identifier, read at the verifying checkpoint, closes the window a lifetime leaves open.

clauses.subject: revocation-id
clauses.statement: Every derivation carries a revocation identifier of its own, so one subtree of delegated authority is withdrawn without ending the root it descends from.

clauses.subject: revocation-epoch
clauses.statement: A revocation epoch scoped on project, tenant and principal class invalidates exactly that slice of outstanding authority. A project-wide bump is the blunt response to a suspected key leak.

clauses.subject: revoked-credential
clauses.statement: A credential whose identifier appears on the denylist, or whose epoch sits below the current scoped epoch, raises `AuthorityRevoked` at the effect about to act.

clauses.subject: denylist-scope
clauses.statement: A denylist entry bounds the interval between a withdrawal and a lapse, and it ages out once the identifier it names can no longer verify under any live key version.

clauses.subject: leak-response
clauses.statement: A suspected leak of signing material runs a project-wide epoch bump together with immediate retirement of the key version, rather than either instrument alone.

clauses.subject: provider-sign-out
clauses.statement: A provider-side sign-out does not reach a credential already minted; the credential's remaining lifetime is what bounds that window. Immediate withdrawal runs on the epoch rather than on the provider's session.

clauses.subject: rotation-grace
clauses.statement: A rotation policy declares a cadence and a grace window during which the retiring key version stays verifiable. The window is validated against the persisted issuance policy rather than against a bare flag.

clauses.subject: short-grace
clauses.statement: A declared grace window shorter than the effective issuance ceiling raises `RotationGraceTooShort`, as does an explicit override below that ceiling. The window covers the whole remaining life of a credential minted an instant before a rotation.

clauses.subject: rotation-is-not-revocation
clauses.statement: A retiring key version verifies for the whole of its grace window by design. Compromise response runs on the scoped epoch and the immediate-retire path, never on waiting for a window to lapse.

clauses.subject: immediate-retire
clauses.statement: Immediate retirement removes a key version from the published set and from every static pin, and a checkpoint picks the removal up at its next refresh.

clauses.subject: format-withdrawal
clauses.statement: Withdrawing a credential format runs through revocation, genuine expiry or issuer-key rotation under a declared compatibility policy. Every admission path stops admitting the withdrawn format at the cutover instant.

clauses.subject: withdrawn-format
clauses.statement: A credential in a withdrawn format raises `CredentialFormatWithdrawn` at every admission path. Restoring acceptance takes an explicit declaration and never happens silently.

clauses.subject: exchange-surface
clauses.statement: The exchange runs as `contextful token exchange` on the command line and as `POST /auth/exchange` on the serving query face, provisioned per project under `.contextful/exchange/`: `policy.toml` holds the exchange policy and `verify.key` holds the injected verifying material. The verified external assertion is the route's own credential.

clauses.subject: exchange-policy
clauses.statement: An exchange policy declares `expected_iss`, an optional `expected_aud`, a `subject_map` from a capability subject member onto a verified claim with an optional `{}` template, a `role_claim`, a `role_grants` map from role value onto grants, `default_grants`, `ttl_secs`, `minted_iss` and `minted_aud`.

clauses.subject: injected-material
clauses.statement: Verifying material is injected by the operator — a shared secret, an RS256 public key in PEM form, or a key-set document from which the key is selected by the assertion header's `kid`. The exchange core performs no network call, which keeps it testable offline.

clauses.subject: read-path-independence
clauses.statement: The identity provider is contacted once, at the mint. Every later read checks the capability credential against pinned key material, so provider downtime does not reach the read path.

clauses.subject: minted-grants
clauses.statement: Minted grants are drawn from the policy's role map and its declared default grants and from nowhere else, so a minted credential is never broader than the policy. A verified role matching no entry earns the default grants, which are empty.

clauses.subject: minted-lifetime-default
clauses.statement: A minted lifetime defaults to 900 s where the policy declares none.

clauses.subject: minted-lifetime-ceiling
clauses.statement: A configured minted lifetime clamps to a ceiling of 3600 s. The clamp reduces and never extends, so a mis-set policy lowers privilege alone.

clauses.subject: minted-audience
clauses.statement: A minted credential carries the deployment audience, so an audience-checking verifier turns back a cross-store replay. A policy naming no audience falls back onto the project's persisted default, and a local development mint stays unbound.

clauses.subject: assertion-invalid
clauses.statement: A bad signature, a lapsed assertion, an untrusted issuer or audience, or a mapped claim absent from the verified assertion mints nothing and raises `ExchangeAssertionInvalid`. Every refusal on this path fails closed.

clauses.subject: missing-material
clauses.statement: An exchange configured with no verifying material raises `ExchangeMaterialMissing` and mints nothing. A stale injected key fails closed at the mint rather than healing itself.

clauses.subject: per-reader-token
clauses.statement: An application embedding the read path holds no project-wide credential. Per request it trades its signed-in reader's verified assertion for that reader's short-lived, least-privilege credential and reads as them.

clauses.subject: no-cross-reader-cache
clauses.statement: An exchanged credential is held against the reader it was minted for and is never reused for a second reader.

clauses.subject: mint-custody
clauses.statement: The root capability lives in the embedding application's backend key custody. A browser, an agent client and anything delivered to a tenant hold a per-request minted credential and nothing more.

clauses.subject: bound-tenancy
clauses.statement: The organization identifier from the verified assertion is stamped into the minted subject's account member, and the filter reading that member is parameter-bound rather than interpolated. Isolation rests on the bound predicate rather than on the mint.

clauses.subject: no-directory
clauses.statement: This engine holds no user directory and consumes no directory-synchronization feed. Tenancy travels per credential, and verifying who a principal acts for is the minting backend's obligation.

clauses.subject: identity-versus-capability
clauses.statement: An external assertion answers who a principal is, which organization they belong to and which roles they hold, with the provider as source of truth. A capability credential answers what a principal does to which tables under which filters, with the manifest as source of truth. They compose as layers, and neither substitutes for the other.

clauses.subject: minted-derivation
clauses.statement: A minted credential derives offline into strictly narrower children for sub-agents, and its confirmation claim binds it to the holder's key pair.

clauses.subject: write-time-removal
clauses.statement: Redaction runs inside the writer ahead of columnar encoding, with two operations selectable per declared rule: a drop, where no cell ever holds the value, and a transform, where a policy-defined substitute — a keyed digest, a token, a prefix, a generalized band — occupies the cell.

clauses.subject: pipeline-wide-rules
clauses.statement: A rule set is declared on a pipeline and binds every table that pipeline lands, child tables included.

clauses.subject: stage-follows-normalization
clauses.statement: The stage runs after relational normalization has shredded structured values into child tables, so a value reachable through a child table alone is reached by the rule naming its parent.

clauses.subject: value-precedes-the-durable-record
clauses.statement: A value this layer removes is absent from the run path's durable record. Replay returns the recorded output and repeats no side effect, so one recording is a permanent recording, and the record rather than the destination is the boundary this layer holds.

clauses.subject: rule-over-a-recorded-source
clauses.statement: Declaring removal rules over a source whose pulls are recorded verbatim raises `EnforceRedactionOnRecordedSource`, before that source is first read.

clauses.subject: refetch-replaces-replay
clauses.statement: A table under removal rules gives up replay-without-refetch: re-running its pipeline reaches the source again.

clauses.subject: stolen-credential-yields-removed-bytes
clauses.statement: A stolen object-store credential yields columnar bytes with the value already gone, for columns handled at write time whose sidecar indexes encrypt under the table's own key-management key.

clauses.subject: query-time-leaves-cleartext
clauses.statement: A column protected at query time alone sits in cleartext inside the stored bytes, and the object-store credential reveals it.

clauses.subject: index-over-a-removed-column
clauses.statement: Declaring a vector graph, a full-text segment set, a bloom filter or a zone map over a column removed at write time raises `EnforceIndexOverRemovedColumn`. An index built from the original values reconstructs what the rule took out.

clauses.subject: summarize-only-retains-the-text
clauses.statement: A column carrying the summarize-only flag stores its text whole, since grounding and citation read that text, and the release bound binds on the way out instead. The flag lands at write time and travels with the column, so a surface added later inherits that bound without consulting the pipeline that produced the rows.

clauses.subject: rules-per-pipeline
clauses.statement: A pipeline carries at most 256 entries in its removal rule set.

clauses.subject: rule-row
clauses.statement: A rule names a table, a column, one operation, and the argument that operation takes.

clauses.subject: three-layers
clauses.statement: The reference monitor is exactly three layers: removal at write time, the redistribution bound at sync, and row-and-column restriction at query time. A request is authorized at each in turn, so a credential stolen at one buys nothing at the next two.

clauses.subject: complete-mediation
clauses.statement: Calling this stack a reference monitor imports the always-invoked obligation. A code path that arrives at stored rows without traversing the layers is a defect by definition and never a documented limitation.

clauses.subject: unmediated-path
clauses.statement: A read arriving at stored rows outside a registered relation raises `EnforceUnmediatedPath`.

clauses.subject: single-owning-module
clauses.statement: One module owns the decision. Where a gateway and the engine reach the same verdict they execute that module, compiled native and compiled to WebAssembly from the same pinned source.

clauses.subject: second-verifier
clauses.statement: A second implementation of any part of this decision, in another language or another crate, raises `EnforceSecondVerifier`.

clauses.subject: protection-is-a-rewrite
clauses.statement: Protection is applied as transformation in the data plane — predicates compiled into the statement, column projections rewritten, a per-token filter at the sync edge, zone floors.

clauses.subject: relation-order
clauses.statement: A registered relation composes, in order: the mirrored permission semi-join, the tenant equality, the row predicate joined against the subject relation, the table policy, the project default, then the column projection.

clauses.subject: conjunctive-narrowing
clauses.statement: Layers conjoin. A row surviving the composition survives each layer taken alone, and appending a layer removes rows and adds none.

clauses.subject: pass-precedes-the-cut
clauses.statement: The single pass completes before the ranked result is cut to its requested size, so the positions a caller sees carry no trace of a withheld row.

clauses.subject: vector-arm-rejoins
clauses.statement: A sidecar vector index is not a relation. Its arm returns candidate identifiers, and those identifiers re-join through the registered relation before the arm contributes anything to a result.

clauses.subject: every-face-reads-the-registration
clauses.statement: Lexical, keyword-scored, vector and fused arms inherit the whole composition beneath the row bound, and an arm added later inherits it without naming it. The resolution carrying it to each arm is {{read.register.invariant.bare-name}}.

clauses.subject: replica-is-constrained-again
clauses.statement: A caller already holding a filtered replica is constrained a second time, per query, with the bytes of that replica unchanged.

clauses.subject: order-is-not-commutative
clauses.statement: Restricting rows on a column and then masking that column differs in result from masking it and then restricting. The composed order is the specified one, and no commutativity is claimed.

clauses.subject: registered-relation
clauses.statement: The compiler emits one relation per granted table, bound to that table's bare name inside the session, for the lifetime of the session.

clauses.subject: session-build
clauses.statement: A session builds its relations at admission from resolved grants, and rebuilds them when a revocation or a manifest change invalidates a grant it holds.

clauses.subject: relations-per-session
clauses.statement: A session carries at most 1024 entries in its relation set.

clauses.subject: mirrored-join-leads
clauses.statement: The permission semi-join derived from a source's own access lists is conjoined ahead of everything the operator wrote. Its construction is [`42-visibility.md` § Mirrored permissions](42-visibility.md); a row the source hides stays hidden whatever the local policy says.

clauses.subject: predicate-grammar
clauses.statement: A row predicate is a typed boolean subset of SQL: column references, comparison operators, conjunction, disjunction, negation, membership lists, pattern matching, null tests, and scalar functions declared safe.

clauses.subject: parsed-at-manifest-load
clauses.statement: Each predicate parses to a tree when the manifest loads, so a malformed one is discovered by the process reading the declaration rather than by the first caller.

clauses.subject: term-outside-the-grammar
clauses.statement: A predicate referencing anything the grammar omits raises `EnforcePredicateOutsideGrammar`, naming the offending node.

clauses.subject: subject-relation
clauses.statement: Subject claims reach a predicate through a session-scoped subject relation, bound as prepared-statement parameters and joined against. A principal value carrying SQL syntax stays a value: it occupies a parameter slot and reaches no parser.

clauses.subject: interpolated-claim
clauses.statement: Splicing a subject claim into SQL text anywhere in the runtime raises `EnforceInterpolatedSubjectClaim`, and the gate rejects the change that introduced it.

clauses.subject: join-pushes-down
clauses.statement: The engine pushes the subject join into the scan, so a restricted scan costs what an unrestricted one costs in the common case.

clauses.subject: narrowing-order
clauses.statement: Predicates narrow in order: the credential's own predicate, then table-level predicates whose subject condition matches, then the project default.

clauses.subject: matched-override
clauses.statement: A table-level predicate declaring an override for a matching subject condition widens its own arm and reaches no other arm of the conjunction.

clauses.subject: default-is-deny
clauses.statement: No grant match yields no rows. A table reached with nothing matching produces an empty result rather than its contents.

clauses.subject: tenant-equality-is-engine-applied
clauses.statement: A tenant-scoped grant compiles a bound-parameter byte equality on the tenant-scope column, conjoined ahead of any table-level policy.

clauses.subject: isolation-survives-a-forgotten-clause
clauses.statement: The tenant equality is never a clause the consumer's statement is trusted to carry, so an author who omits one loses no isolation and a consumer keeps one isolation control instead of two, deleting its own per-row re-check.

clauses.subject: exception-condition
clauses.statement: A predicate carries exception conditions written as boolean expressions over subject fields, parsed by the grammar above and bound by the same parameter mechanism.

clauses.subject: predicate-size
clauses.statement: A single declared predicate holds at most 4 KiB of source text.

clauses.subject: membership-list
clauses.statement: A membership list inside a predicate holds at most 512 entries.

clauses.subject: strategies
clauses.statement: Six strategies exist: drop, keyed hash, format-preserving tokenization, truncation to a leading character count, bucketing into a generalized band, and numeric range generalization.

clauses.subject: summarize-only
clauses.statement: A seventh declaration is a flag rather than a strategy: summarize-only keeps the value legible to grounding and citation while bounding what any surface releases verbatim.

clauses.subject: verbatim-quote
clauses.statement: A summarize-only column releases at most 280 chars of its value verbatim in one citation.

clauses.subject: no-surface-exceeds-the-quote
clauses.statement: The contract every read surface satisfies is that republishable prose past the quote bound leaves none of them. Whether quoting a licensed source is permissible at all is the publisher's own adjudication.

clauses.subject: drop-yields-null
clauses.statement: Drop nulls the cell, and yields an empty string where the column's type is a string.

clauses.subject: primary-and-combine-are-one-value
clauses.statement: A complete mask is a single value whose primary half and secondary half are both private. A consumer holding one has no route to apply the primary alone, so discarding a mandated secondary fails to compile.

clauses.subject: one-value-two-layers
clauses.statement: That same value drives the write-time layer and the query-time layer, so a declared combine cannot reach one of them and miss the other.

clauses.subject: digest-alone-over-an-exhaustible-class
clauses.statement: A keyed hash standing alone over a column declared a national identifier, a phone number, an email address or a medical record number raises `EnforceDigestAloneOnExhaustibleClass`. Those value spaces are enumerable end to end, and a project pepper is stolen by whoever steals the column it protects.

clauses.subject: high-entropy-hashes-alone
clauses.statement: A column whose values are random identifiers or opaque tokens carries a keyed hash with no secondary.

clauses.subject: combine-without-generalization
clauses.statement: Bucketing or numeric range generalization layered behind a hash or a tokenization raises `EnforceCombineWithoutGeneralization`: both act on numbers, a digest is hexadecimal text, and the pairing leaves the primary's output untouched.

clauses.subject: truncation-generalizes-a-digest
clauses.statement: Truncation is the one secondary that generalizes a digest. Cutting to a leading hexadecimal run collapses many inputs onto one output, so an exhaustive search over an enumerable domain returns a crowd rather than a person.

clauses.subject: hash-truncation-width
clauses.statement: A truncation behind a keyed hash carries a width below 32 chars.

clauses.subject: token-truncation-width
clauses.statement: A truncation behind a tokenization carries a width below 20 chars.

clauses.subject: truncation-that-cuts-nothing
clauses.statement: A declared width at or past the primary's own output width raises `EnforceTruncationCutsNothing`. How narrow a width collapses enough against the column's real value space stays the operator's judgment, since the manifest declares no domain size.

clauses.subject: project-pepper
clauses.statement: One environment variable supplies the key for hashing and tokenization, read by both layers through a single resolved value.

clauses.subject: development-fallback-is-loud
clauses.statement: Left unset, that variable resolves to a constant present in the source tree — making masked values reversible over any enumerable domain — and the process emits one signal per run rather than proceeding quietly.

clauses.subject: digest-joins-across-layers
clauses.statement: Both layers compute the same keyed digest, natively where bytes are written and as an expression inside the relation where they are read, so a value masked at one layer joins against the same value masked at the other. That expression carries the key-derived pad blocks in the relation body, leaving the pepper legible to anyone reading the session catalog.

clauses.subject: subject-exception
clauses.statement: A mask carries its own exceptions, each a condition on the subject written in the row-predicate grammar and bound through the subject relation, with no splicing into text.

clauses.subject: columns-replaced-in-place
clauses.statement: The masked projection substitutes named columns where they stand rather than listing a declared schema, since a union projects provenance columns no declared schema names. The column set a caller receives, and its order, match what the same statement produces unmasked.

clauses.subject: star-expands-to-the-masked-projection
clauses.statement: A star projection expands to the masked projection, so a caller receives masked values instead of an error.

clauses.subject: equality-on-a-dropped-column
clauses.statement: An equality filter against a dropped column matches nothing, since the comparison runs against null. A keyed hash is the strategy that keeps equality filtering available.

clauses.subject: aggregates-read-the-masked-column
clauses.statement: Aggregation runs over the masked column, and the two generalizing strategies keep an aggregate close to the one the original values produce.

clauses.subject: mask-on-an-absent-column
clauses.statement: A declared mask naming a column the table's schema omits raises `EnforceMaskOnAbsentColumn` at manifest load.

clauses.subject: masks-per-table
clauses.statement: A table carries at most 128 entries in its column mask set.

clauses.subject: out-of-scope-read
clauses.statement: A credential scoped to one tenant reading another tenant's rows on a granted table raises `EnforceScopeDenied`, carried as wire code `scope_denied`, HTTP 403, and an in-band tool error on the tool protocol, naming the table, the granted scope and the requested one.

clauses.subject: no-empty-result-substitution
clauses.statement: That case produces the typed error and never an empty result set, so a caller distinguishes a boundary from a quiet table.

clauses.subject: requested-value-echoes-the-statement
clauses.statement: The requested value in the error echoes what the statement asked for, never a value read from storage, so the refusal discloses nothing about any other tenant.

clauses.subject: ungranted-table
clauses.statement: A table the caller holds no grant on raises `EnforceUnknownRelation`: it is absent from listings, absent from descriptions, and reads as a name nothing is bound to.

clauses.subject: grant-is-not-an-existence-oracle
clauses.statement: Holding a grant never becomes a way to enumerate what exists beyond it. The ungranted case and the out-of-scope case answer differently for that purpose.

clauses.subject: error-payload
clauses.statement: A refusal payload carries at most 512 B.

clauses.subject: scope-guard-surfaces
clauses.statement: The scope guard decides one walk over the engine's own parse and covers two caller surfaces: a literal equality or membership list in the statement's tree, and a bound template parameter destined for the tenant column.

clauses.subject: top-level-conjuncts-only
clauses.statement: The guard reads top-level conjuncts, since a disjunct constrains no whole predicate, and reads them only for a statement whose own FROM names a scoped table, so a common table expression rebinding the column name is not mistaken for the tenant column.

clauses.subject: guard-walk
clauses.statement: The guard visits at most 4096 entries of one parse tree.

clauses.subject: undecidable-shapes-compose
clauses.statement: A constraint the guard cannot settle — a range, a pattern match — composes with the engine-applied equality as an ordinary conjunct. The equality, and not the guard, is what isolates.

clauses.subject: drifted-scope-reads-empty
clauses.statement: A tenant value matching no partition is indistinguishable at read time from a tenant that wrote nothing: both produce an empty result. Byte identity of a scope value is settled when a credential is minted and when a manifest is built, and the read path repairs no value an upstream step transformed.

clauses.subject: cleared-flag-withholds
clauses.statement: A per-table redistribution flag cleared holds back every object of that table at push and keeps the table's name out of the manifest written to the bucket. A list of keys discloses a table's existence, its run identifiers and its freshness, so the manifest omits the name rather than carrying it with no objects behind it.

clauses.subject: exclusion-precedes-the-diff
clauses.statement: The exclusion applies before the object diff is computed, so a withheld object is never read-then-skipped and no later push catches it up.

clauses.subject: licence-outranks-a-full-grant
clauses.statement: The bound holds against a credential granted everything, since what it constrains is redistribution rather than authority.

clauses.subject: two-envelopes-carry-rows
clauses.statement: Rows travel in two envelopes: the table's own columnar files, and the verbatim record each pull writes. Both are in scope for the bound.

clauses.subject: root-object-allowlist
clauses.statement: While any table is withheld, a root-level object ships when it is proven free of row data. The mirrored permission tables and the stale-memory index ship; the catalog database, the durable-record blob directory and the memory database stay behind.

clauses.subject: root-object-outside-the-allowlist
clauses.statement: A root-level object absent from that allowlist raises `EnforceRootObjectNotAllowlisted` at push. The list enumerates what ships rather than what stays, so an object added by someone who never read this rule stays behind.

clauses.subject: objects-left-behind
clauses.statement: Clearing the flag over a table an earlier unrestricted push uploaded raises `EnforceStaleRedistributedObjects`, naming each object and the remedy, and removing none of them. The refusal persists while any uploaded record may carry that table's rows.

clauses.subject: manifest-is-an-index
clauses.statement: An object stays fetchable by its key after the manifest stops naming it: a manifest indexes objects and authorizes nothing.

clauses.subject: reported-objects
clauses.statement: A left-behind report names at most 100 files and states the total it found.

clauses.subject: detector-window-is-narrowed
clauses.statement: The check runs twice per push, once ahead of the upload loop and once after it. Two passes narrow rather than close the window against a second writer active at the same moment under a different configuration, and the guarantee rests on a deployment holding one bucket and one pushing configuration rather than on arbitration between writers that disagree.

clauses.subject: sync-edge-filter
clauses.statement: A serving edge in front of the bucket filters a materialized replica by the pulling credential's grants, so the bucket holds the write-time-handled data whole and each replica receives the slices its credential admits. The edge is the control for a column that stays queryable in some replicas and not in others, where removal at write time reaches too far.

clauses.subject: zone-constructors
clauses.statement: A zone is one of five constructors: a local device, an on-premises environment with an identifier, a private cloud with an account identifier, a public cloud with an opaque vendor identifier, and undeclared. The identifier is part of the value rather than a label beside it.

clauses.subject: zone-string
clauses.statement: A zone string parses, after trimming, as `local:device`, `on-prem:<id>`, `private-cloud:<id>` or `public-cloud:<id>`. Any other text parses as undeclared.

clauses.subject: allow-set-pattern
clauses.statement: An allow-set entry is `*`, `local:device`, `on-prem:*`, `private-cloud:*`, `public-cloud:*`, or a category prefix carrying a concrete identifier.

clauses.subject: unparsed-pattern
clauses.statement: An allow-set entry matching no pattern form raises `EnforceZonePatternUnparsed`, naming the entry, rather than becoming a pattern that silently matches nothing.

clauses.subject: allow-set-is-disjunctive
clauses.statement: A zone is admitted when any entry matches it. A bare category entry matches every identifier in its category; an entry carrying an identifier matches that identifier alone.

clauses.subject: undeclared-is-most-restrictive
clauses.statement: An explicit `*` is the one entry admitting an undeclared zone. No category entry admits it, a public-cloud entry included.

clauses.subject: zone-belongs-to-the-caller
clauses.statement: A zone is a short tag describing where the consuming model runs, carried by the client process making the call and not by the store it reads.

clauses.subject: policy-picks-no-model
clauses.statement: Placement policy selects no model, assembles no prompt and dispatches no inference call. The one invocation point inside the engine is an operator-configured endpoint capability the synthesis step uses.

clauses.subject: vendor-client-library
clauses.statement: A model-vendor client library linked into any crate raises `EnforceVendorClientLibrary`, checked on every change. What the system owns is the caller's declared zone and the zone the data admits.

clauses.subject: two-questions-compose
clauses.statement: Authority answers who reads what; placement answers where the answer is processed. One session legitimately holds both a grant over protected records and a key to a public-cloud model, and those records stay inside the on-premises boundary.

clauses.subject: unlabeled-table-fails-closed
clauses.statement: A table declaring no zone policy resolves to the fail-closed pair — a local device and an on-premises environment — and reaches no cloud category until an operator widens it deliberately.

clauses.subject: permissive-default-with-several-principals
clauses.statement: A permissive default resolving an unlabeled table to `*` raises `EnforcePermissiveZoneDefault` wherever more than one principal owns the store. It stands where a single principal owns everything.

clauses.subject: floor-covers-discovered-tables
clauses.statement: A capability read session applies the fail-closed resolution to declared tables and to tables discovered after startup, synthesized memory among them.

clauses.subject: protected-class-floor
clauses.statement: A column or table classified as protected health information carries an implicit floor at the fail-closed pair, and a declared set wider than that floor resolves down to it when a read is served.

clauses.subject: floor-widened-without-an-override
clauses.statement: A manifest widening a protected-class surface past its floor raises `EnforceProtectedFloorWidened` unless it carries the explicit override flag.

clauses.subject: removal-with-public-cloud
clauses.statement: A surface declaring write-time removal on a column and an allow-set admitting a public cloud raises `EnforceRemovalWithPublicCloud`. The two declarations state opposite intent about one surface.

clauses.subject: narrowest-grain-wins
clauses.statement: A column's set narrows its table's; a principal's set narrows both.

clauses.subject: excluded-cell-is-null
clauses.statement: A cell whose effective set omits the session's zone arrives null, including where a mask exception otherwise reveals it.

clauses.subject: excluded-row-is-withheld
clauses.statement: Where the table's effective set omits the session's zone, the whole row leaves the result.

clauses.subject: per-principal-policy
clauses.statement: A principal declaration carries an allow-set of its own, so a row authored by a principal pinned to local processing stays pinned wherever that row lands, a table declaring `*` included, with no consumer aware of the pin. A row carrying no verified author resolves as restrictively as an undeclared zone.

clauses.subject: evidence-floor
clauses.statement: A synthesized row's declared set is legal at or beneath the intersection of the sets its evidence tables carry: a zone is admitted where every evidence table admits it.

clauses.subject: declaration-above-the-evidence-floor
clauses.statement: A synthesized row declaring a set wider than that intersection raises `EnforceEvidenceFloorExceeded` and resolves to the intersection.

clauses.subject: incognito-pins-the-session
clauses.statement: Incognito — one toggle in the desktop client, one command-line flag, one request field — pins the session to the fail-closed pair, so a row admitting neither of those two leaves the result and nothing crosses the machine boundary.

clauses.subject: widening-under-incognito
clauses.statement: A session asserting a zone wider than the pin raises `EnforceIncognitoWidening`.

clauses.subject: incognito-binds-the-local-owner
clauses.statement: Incognito applies zone resolution to the uncredentialed local owner's reads, which are otherwise unrestricted.

clauses.subject: team-default
clauses.statement: A project declares a default zone and whether a user widens it. An administrator sets incognito as the team-wide default, and an individual turns it off per session where their capability grants that.

clauses.subject: wildcard-on-the-subject-side
clauses.statement: A credential granting a wildcard zone raises `EnforceWildcardZoneOnSubject` at issuance. A wildcard belongs to the data's declaration.

clauses.subject: excluded-rows-leave-before-the-cut
clauses.statement: Zone-excluded rows leave a hybrid result before it is cut to size, so a caller infers nothing about the rank of a row the zone forbids.

clauses.subject: serve-time-outcome
clauses.statement: Serving one row yields a drop-row flag and a list of masked column names. A table set excluding the session drops the row; a column whose narrower set excludes the session is masked while the row is served.

clauses.subject: response-envelope
clauses.statement: The envelope carries the count of rows removed by predicate, the count removed by zone, the names of columns masked by policy, the names masked by zone, the session's asserted zone, and the incognito flag.

clauses.subject: envelope-carries-no-content
clauses.statement: The envelope reports that filtering happened and carries no value that filtering removed.

clauses.subject: inclusion-is-symbolic
clauses.statement: Inclusion against a floor is decided over every constructor and every identifier, and never by probing a fixed set of example zones.

clauses.subject: allow-set-entries
clauses.statement: An allow-set holds at most 32 entries.

clauses.subject: zone-identifier-length
clauses.statement: A zone identifier holds at most 128 chars.

clauses.subject: claim-defends-against-accident
clauses.statement: The zone claim sits on the footing of the agent and host fields: a compromised client asserts whatever it likes. What it buys is a boundary against a user who switched to a public endpoint with private context loaded, plus an audit record where every read carries the zone asserted at the time.

clauses.subject: placement-meets-data-placement
clauses.statement: A proxy-mode replica resolves zones at the proxy boundary, so a table barred from a laptop is also not served from the proxy to a public cloud. A full replica on a laptop serves a locally-tagged row to a local device and withholds the same row from a public cloud on that same machine. A query running inside a private cloud consumes data tagged for that account through the deploy-time tag linking host to zone.

clauses.subject: excluded-concerns
clauses.statement: Model routing, gateway behavior, cryptographic proof of a zone, per-row zone tags and inference cost accounting are undefined here. A routing component reuses this vocabulary from outside the data plane; a mixed-sensitivity table is handled by a row predicate; the audit fields are sufficient input for an external cost report.

clauses.subject: data-plane-is-the-operators
clauses.statement: Columnar files, the manifest and the catalog database live in a bucket the deploying organization controls. No vendor-operated data path exists.

clauses.subject: control-plane-holds-no-rows
clauses.statement: An optional hosted control plane stores manifests and schedules, and stores no row of any table.

clauses.subject: region-allow-set
clauses.statement: A residency policy carries a set of regions. Placement in a region is permitted where the set is empty, meaning unconstrained, or where it names that region. The check reads the declared set and the candidate region and consults nothing else.

clauses.subject: region-mismatch
clauses.statement: A configured resource resolving to a region the policy omits raises `EnforceRegionMismatch` at startup, and the runtime does not begin serving.

clauses.subject: air-gapped-operation
clauses.statement: A single-node daemon runs against local storage with no external store, and a multi-node cluster runs against an on-premises catalog. Neither path reaches the public internet.

clauses.subject: region-entries
clauses.statement: A residency allow-set holds at most 16 entries.

clauses.subject: enforcement-sits-below-the-prompt
clauses.statement: The permission semi-join and the row and column restrictions are compiled into the relation the caller reads, so a fully compromised model asks and the relation answers inside the caller's scope. No part of that path is expressed as text an ingested document can argue with, leaving persuasion no target.

clauses.subject: ingested-content-is-grounding
clauses.statement: Ingested content carries provenance and is grounding material rather than instruction, whatever imperative form its text takes.

clauses.subject: credential-shaped-value
clauses.statement: The write path raises `EnforceCredentialShapedValue` on a value matching a credential shape, before that value reaches storage.

clauses.subject: org-face-is-read-only
clauses.statement: An organization-wide face serves the read subset of the tool surface, and the sanctioned writes on the conversational path are server-authored, so an injected instruction finds no write tool to reach for.

clauses.subject: write-tool-on-a-read-face
clauses.statement: Registering a write tool on an organization-wide face raises `EnforceWriteOnReadOnlyFace`.

clauses.subject: ingest-is-not-egress
clauses.statement: Connector host access is capability-declared and allowlisted, so a connector built for an internal API reaches no arbitrary external host even under injection, and a zone pin over a sensitive table binds where the summarizing model runs, so "summarize this" cannot become "send this to a public endpoint".

clauses.subject: residue-is-bounded
clauses.statement: Injection still steers an answer inside the reader's own scope — misleading them, or surfacing something in-scope they did not ask about. The conjunction bounds that harm rather than removing it, and masks and the summarize-only bound still apply on the way out, so the most sensitive columns are not reproduced word for word even for a reader allowed to ground on them.

clauses.subject: classifier-is-not-the-control
clauses.statement: A classifier placed in front of the model is not the enforcement point, and no clause here depends on one.

clauses.subject: twin-api-as-a-source
clauses.statement: An API licensed to see what no individual user sees — security, eDiscovery, legal-hold export — raises `EnforceTwinApiSource` for every source, since using one lifts the system's ceiling above every human's. A sanctioned, paid, disclosed organization-wide export path is admitted; the line is the licence and the resulting ceiling.

clauses.subject: two-key-rule
clauses.statement: A row reaches a subject exactly when three conjuncts hold together: the mirrored source access list grants it, manifest policy grants it, and the caller's credential grants it. No layer unions, no administrative override widens, and no cached term survives its own invalidation.

clauses.subject: source-faithful-audience
