clauses.statement: Mirroring reproduces the audience the originating system drew, including an audience wider than anyone intended. Manifest policy is the single place where need-to-know narrows further, and it is data in the manifest, read as a diff.

clauses.subject: unknown-class-is-invisible
clauses.statement: A resource whose access list failed to mirror carries `visibility_class = 'unknown'` and reaches no subject at all, an operator holding a deployment-wide credential included, until manifest policy names it.

clauses.subject: access-tables
clauses.statement: The mirror is `access_resources` (one row per governed object), `access_grants` (one row per resource, principal and level), `access_principals`, `access_group_members` (one edge of the group graph), `access_identity_links`, `access_tombstones` (one observed revocation) and `access_freshness`.

clauses.subject: access-table-count
clauses.statement: The mirror is 7 entries in the table namespace and gains an eighth by an amendment to this clause.

clauses.subject: resource-row
clauses.statement: `access_resources` carries `resource_id`, `source`, `resource_kind`, `container_id`, `visibility_class`, and the observation columns every access row shares.

clauses.subject: grant-row
clauses.statement: `access_grants` carries `resource_id`, `principal`, `principal_kind` and `level`, one row per distinct triple, with the observation columns alongside.

clauses.subject: principal-row
clauses.statement: `access_principals` carries `principal`, `principal_kind` and the source's own label for it; `access_group_members` carries `group`, `member` and `member_kind`, one row per edge.

clauses.subject: identity-link-row
clauses.statement: `access_identity_links` carries `source_principal`, `subject`, `method` and `confidence`, mapping one source account onto one workspace subject.

clauses.subject: tombstone-row
clauses.statement: `access_tombstones` carries `scope`, `resource_id`, `principal`, `level` and `revoked_at`, each key part a typed column rather than a packed string. `scope` takes one of `resource`, `grant`, `principal`.

clauses.subject: freshness-row
clauses.statement: `access_freshness` carries one row per source and sweep kind: the enforced `watermark_at` beside the diagnostic `last_full_sweep_at`, `last_incremental_at`, `lag_seconds` and `budget_seconds`.

clauses.subject: watermark-is-the-enforced-field
clauses.statement: Of the freshness columns, `watermark_at` alone decides a read; the remaining fields inform an operator and decide nothing.

clauses.subject: principal-kind
clauses.statement: `principal_kind` takes one of `user`, `group`, `team`, `channel`, `org`, `public`, and a source vocabulary outside that set is normalized onto it by the mapping.

clauses.subject: public-principal-is-literal
clauses.statement: The principal spelled `public` is an ordinary row in the grant table, and every request carries it alongside the subject's own principals.

clauses.subject: grant-level-is-opaque
clauses.statement: `level` is a source-defined string — `read`, `write`, `admin`, `triage` — that the mapping projects onto engine actions. A level conferring no read is mirrored for the diagnostic trace and contributes nothing to a reachable set.

clauses.subject: visibility-class
clauses.statement: `visibility_class` takes one of `mirrored`, `coarse`, `federated`, `unknown`, and is recorded per resource: one workspace's open rooms observe cleanly while its private ones do not.

clauses.subject: observed-classes
clauses.statement: The observed class vocabulary holds 4 entries and admits no per-source extension.

clauses.subject: visibility-block
clauses.statement: A content table declares `[pipeline.tables.visibility]` with `source`, `resource_key` (the column naming the governed object), `resource_kind` (the source's own grain), `fidelity`, an optional `family`, `max_acl_staleness` and `on_stale`.

clauses.subject: binding-travels-with-the-table
clauses.statement: The binding belongs to the table and arrives with the pack that lands it, so a face added later inherits it rather than declaring it. One table carries one binding and one governing regime.

clauses.subject: semi-join-is-compiled-in
clauses.statement: The engine compiles a semi-join against the caller's reachable resource set into that caller's registered view. The filter lives in the relation, so structured statements, each retrieval arm, previews, templates and every embedded surface inherit it without restating it.

clauses.subject: view-bypass
clauses.statement: A read path that reaches table rows around the registered view raises `VisibilityViewBypass`, naming the face and the table. There is no supported route past the relation for speed.

clauses.subject: face-turns-organization-wide
clauses.statement: A deployment becomes an organization-wide face at the moment any table declares a visibility block or any permission sweep exists for any source.

clauses.subject: unbound-table
clauses.statement: On an organization-wide face, a table carrying no visibility block raises `VisibilityUnboundTable` from the diagnose command and from the serving guardrail at start, naming the table.

clauses.subject: incomplete-binding
clauses.statement: A binding at a servable level without a declared sweep for its source, or without `max_acl_staleness`, raises `VisibilityBindingIncomplete`. Nothing else produces the source's access rows, and an unmeasured budget enforces nothing.

clauses.subject: excluded-is-the-opt-out
clauses.statement: `fidelity = "excluded"` is the one explicit way a table sits on an organization-wide face without a servable binding, and it states that the table is neither ingested nor queried.

clauses.subject: sweep-kind
clauses.statement: Every access row carries `_acl_sweep_kind` in `full`, `incremental`, `webhook` and `_acl_sweep_id` identifying the run that wrote it. Both the coverage rule and the revocation rule branch on that kind.

clauses.subject: sweep-kinds
clauses.statement: The sweep kind vocabulary holds 3 entries.

clauses.subject: observation-clock
clauses.statement: Every access row carries `_acl_observed_at`, the instant the permission state was read at the source, held separately from the instant the row landed in the store.

clauses.subject: authorization-ages-on-its-own-clock
clauses.statement: A content pull at one hour reusing a sweep from an earlier hour serves aged authorization over fresh content. The separate observation clock is what makes that age computable.

clauses.subject: watermark-covers-everything
clauses.statement: `watermark_at` moves on a sweep run that finished having read every governed resource in the source. Lag is measured from it, so the enforced figure bounds the worst resource rather than the best one.

clauses.subject: partial-run-moves-nothing
clauses.statement: A sweep that failed or covered part of the estate advances no watermark. A limping sweep therefore ages the whole source instead of appearing current on the resources it managed to read.

clauses.subject: deny-outranks-allow
clauses.statement: A tombstone suppresses its resource or its grant for every read after `revoked_at`, whatever a later observation says, until an allow arrives on a full run whose observation instant is newer than the revocation.

clauses.subject: incremental-never-restores
clauses.statement: An observation of the `incremental` or `webhook` kind adds a grant that no tombstone covers and lifts no suppression. Proving one row was seen is not proving the estate was walked.

clauses.subject: tombstone-match-is-typed
clauses.statement: `scope` decides which of `resource_id`, `principal` and `level` participate, so suppression is an equality over typed columns against the grant table rather than a comparison of opaque keys.

clauses.subject: tombstone-scopes
clauses.statement: The tombstone scope vocabulary holds 3 entries.

clauses.subject: revocation-skips-the-content-pull
clauses.statement: Withdrawing a share takes effect on the first read after its sweep commits, with no re-ingestion and no deletion of content rows. Reachability is a join rather than a property baked into the row.

clauses.subject: events-tighten-rows
clauses.statement: A webhook or incremental observation narrows the individual rows it touches the moment it lands.

clauses.subject: ungapped-stream
clauses.statement: Moving `watermark_at` from an event stream that the mapping has not declared gap-detectable — sequenced delivery with reconciliation on a detected gap — raises `VisibilityUngappedStream`. A source without that property lives at its full-run cadence.

clauses.subject: gap-reconciliation
clauses.statement: A gap-detectable stream numbers its deliveries, detects a missing number, and reconciles the affected resources against the source before the watermark advances past the gap.

clauses.subject: sweep-block
clauses.statement: An `[[acl_sweep]]` block declares one governed source's permission sweep: the source key, the credential reference, the resource enumeration, the cadence per sweep kind, and the event stream where one exists.

clauses.subject: orphan-grant
clauses.statement: A grant row landing with no resource row, or whose resource carries the unknown class, raises `VisibilityOrphanGrant` at commit and contributes to no reachable set.

clauses.subject: sweep-writes-through-the-run-path
clauses.statement: Access rows land through the same journaled run path as content, so an observation is replayable, attributable and readable by any tool that opens the store.

clauses.subject: resolution-order
clauses.statement: Per request the engine resolves the credential's verified person to a subject, the subject to source principals through identity links, those principals to a group closure, and principals plus closure plus `public` to resources through grants joined onto resource rows, dropping the unknown class and subtracting tombstones in force.

clauses.subject: verified-methods-authorize
clauses.statement: The join consumes links whose `method` is `scim_email` or `oidc_sub`. A link recorded as `operator_asserted` appears in the diagnostic trace and adds no resource.

clauses.subject: unverified-link-in-the-join
clauses.statement: A link whose method sits outside the verified set reaching the reachable-set computation raises `VisibilityUnverifiedLink`, naming the method and the source.

clauses.subject: links-come-from-provisioning
clauses.statement: {{authority.identify.invariant.directory-link}}

clauses.subject: confidence-relaxes-nothing
clauses.statement: `confidence` is recorded beside the method and enters no threshold. A link either carries a verified method or contributes nothing.

clauses.subject: unlinked-subject-reads-nothing
clauses.statement: A subject with no resolved principal in a source reads none of that source rather than all of it, so a mapping gap lands as a denial.

clauses.subject: principal-kinds
clauses.statement: A reachable set is built from principals of 6 entries in the kind vocabulary, the literal `public` among them.

clauses.subject: group-closure-depth
clauses.statement: The closure walks the group graph to `max_group_depth`, default 8 hops, declared per deployment.

clauses.subject: closure-over-depth
clauses.statement: A closure reaching the depth bound raises `VisibilityClosureDepth` (HTTP 503) and returns no set. Truncation narrows in silence and produces an answer indistinguishable from a complete one.

clauses.subject: org-membership-is-an-edge
clauses.statement: A mapping normalizes organization membership into the group edge table with the organization as a node, so a grant to an `org` principal matches like any other group grant rather than sitting unmatched.

clauses.subject: expansion-is-late
clauses.statement: The closure runs at read time over the mirrored graph rather than being folded into the content index at write time. Membership turns over far faster than documents do.

clauses.subject: materialization-shares-invalidation
clauses.statement: A materialized closure is keyed on the same epochs as the request-time walk, making it an optimization with identical invalidation rather than a second account of who belongs to what.

clauses.subject: cache-key
clauses.statement: The reachable-set cache key is the subject, a source epoch over grants, resources, tombstones and freshness, and a directory epoch over the group graph and identity links.

clauses.subject: equal-key-means-equal-inputs
clauses.statement: Equal cache keys imply identical committed access state by construction, so a revocation rotates the key and the superseded entry is never read again.

clauses.subject: caching-a-degraded-result
clauses.statement: Storing a reachable set or a result produced past a budget, or produced under the narrowing posture, raises `VisibilityDegradedCached`. Those paths pay full cost on every request.

clauses.subject: budget-grammar
clauses.statement: `max_acl_staleness` is a positive integer followed by one suffix from `s`, `m`, `h`, `d` — `90s`, `15m`, `1h`, `2d`.

clauses.subject: malformed-budget
clauses.statement: A compound form, a bare number, or a suffix outside the four raises `VisibilityBudgetMalformed`, naming the table and the text it read. An ambiguous budget is settled by the author rather than by a default.

clauses.subject: budget-is-per-table
clauses.statement: Each table declares its own budget: a conversation corpus at fifteen minutes beside a code corpus at one hour is a coherent posture for one deployment.

clauses.subject: manifest-outranks-the-pack
clauses.statement: A pack ships a budget default per table and the operator's manifest value takes precedence over it wherever both exist.

clauses.subject: lag-reads-the-watermark
clauses.statement: The lag compared against a budget is the distance from `watermark_at` to the request instant, one figure per source, evaluated without joining candidate rows to their own observation ages.

clauses.subject: every-touched-table-is-checked
clauses.statement: A statement spanning several bound tables is checked against each of their budgets, and the tightest governing figure decides the outcome.

clauses.subject: over-budget-read
clauses.statement: A read whose source lag exceeds a touched table's budget raises `VisibilityAccessStale` (HTTP 503, in band on the tool surface) carrying the source, the lag in seconds, the budget in seconds and the last observation instant.

clauses.subject: never-swept-source
clauses.statement: A source with no completed full run raises `VisibilityAccessStale` whatever budget its table declares, carrying a lag the mirror cannot bound. Unswept is maximally aged rather than exempt.

clauses.subject: loudness-over-emptiness
clauses.statement: An aged-authorization outcome is a refusal rather than a shortened result set. An empty answer is an ordinary outcome — a quiet repository, a narrow reader — and a shortened set reads as healthy indefinitely.

clauses.subject: stale-posture
clauses.statement: `on_stale` takes `refuse` or `public_only`, declared per table beside the budget.

clauses.subject: stale-postures
clauses.statement: The posture vocabulary holds 2 entries.

clauses.subject: default-posture-is-refusal
clauses.statement: `on_stale` defaults to `refuse`; the availability posture is opted into per table and disclosed on every answer it touches.

clauses.subject: public-only
clauses.statement: Past the budget, `public_only` serves rows whose resource had its public status re-read within budget by a single-field probe, marking the envelope and the audit record as degraded.

clauses.subject: aged-public-probe
clauses.statement: Where the probe itself sits past the budget, the narrowing posture closes and the read raises `VisibilityAccessStale`. The opened path is never wider than the closed one.

clauses.subject: narrowing-not-exemption
clauses.statement: The availability posture removes rows from what a fresh read returns and adds none, so a resource made private after the last full run is absent rather than served on an aged allow.

clauses.subject: budget-below-cadence
clauses.statement: A budget tighter than the sweep cadence its source sustains raises `VisibilityBudgetUnreachable` at diagnose, naming both figures. A per-item permission model under request limits moves its watermark in hours, and the declaration states that.

clauses.subject: budget-and-cadence-are-one-contract
clauses.statement: The declared budget and the declared sweep cadence are read together at diagnose, so an operator defends the pair rather than the number alone.

clauses.subject: declared-levels
clauses.statement: `fidelity` takes `mirrored` (per-principal lists at the grain the source enforces, joined exactly), `coarse` (a container or workspace signal joined at that grain), `federated` (queried live under the reader's own delegated credential) or `excluded` (no safe path).

clauses.subject: declared-levels
clauses.statement: The declared fidelity vocabulary holds 4 entries.

clauses.subject: servable-levels
clauses.statement: Rows are served out of the store at `mirrored` and at `coarse`. The other two levels describe tables the store never answers from.

clauses.subject: two-distinct-ladders
clauses.statement: The declared level is the operator's claim about what a source supports and bottoms out at `excluded`; the observed class is what a run found per resource and bottoms out at `unknown`. They are separate types and never compared as one.

clauses.subject: coarse-carries-its-grain
clauses.statement: A `coarse` binding puts the source's own grain name into the response envelope, so a reader is told the scope of the approximation rather than the fact of it.

clauses.subject: source-families
clauses.statement: `family` takes `container-roster` (content inherits a membership list), `item-exception` (a container base with per-item breaks), `person-container` (the container is one human being) or `directory` (records about people rather than content).

clauses.subject: source-families
clauses.statement: The source family vocabulary holds 4 entries.

clauses.subject: level-outside-the-family
clauses.statement: A `person-container` table declared at a servable level, and a `directory` table declared above `excluded`, raise `VisibilityFamilyBound` and the table does not load. Classification is a judgment made once; the bound downstream of it is mechanical.

clauses.subject: family-undeclared
clauses.statement: A mapping that lands a table without naming its family raises `VisibilityFamilyUndeclared`. An unnamed family leaves the level claim resting on reviewer judgment alone.

clauses.subject: federated-rows-stay-outside
clauses.statement: A `federated` resource is swept into the resource table holding zero grants, and its content rows enter no store table, so no credential of any breadth surfaces them.

clauses.subject: federated-table-registered
clauses.statement: Registering a `federated` table on a read face raises `VisibilityFederatedRegistered`. Its observable effect is the resource's absence, and the trace prints the class so the absence reads as the level rather than as a missing grant.

clauses.subject: federated-cache-shared
clauses.statement: Retaining a federated result under a key that omits the subject raises `VisibilityFederatedCacheShared`. That result was authorized by one reader's own delegated credential and belongs to no other.

clauses.subject: hybrid-answer-legs
clauses.statement: An answer drawn from both the mirror and a live query marks the leg on each citation, lists the federated sources consulted, and names the ones that failed or timed out, so a reader learns which part of the question went unanswered.

clauses.subject: computed-access-federates
clauses.statement: Where a source decides access with a sharing engine rather than storing it, the engine's decisions are queried live and its inputs are not reproduced. Reproducing the inputs re-implements the engine, and each drifted edge is a disclosure.

clauses.subject: mirroring-computed-inputs
clauses.statement: A mapping projecting a sharing engine's inputs into `access_grants` raises `VisibilityComputedInputsMirrored`, naming the source.

clauses.subject: a-people-list-is-not-a-roster
clauses.statement: Attendees, invitees, recipients and contacts arriving inside a content payload describe interest rather than entitlement. Attending a meeting confers no read on the note, and appearing on a deal confers no read on the record.

clauses.subject: roster-from-a-payload
clauses.statement: A mapping deriving grants from a people list in the content rather than from the source's permission endpoint raises `VisibilityRosterFromPayload`. The test a mapping passes is whether the source enforces the list at sign-in.

clauses.subject: excluded-is-absent
clauses.statement: An `excluded` table is neither pulled into the store nor queried live, and no surface offers it.

clauses.subject: pack-contents
clauses.statement: A pack is a manifest fragment plus a connector pin declaring: the content tables with their cursors and transforms, the access mapping, fidelity and budget defaults per table, the sweep jobs with their cadences, and the surface templates.

clauses.subject: pack-is-data
clauses.statement: A pack carries configuration read as a diff and carries no executable logic of its own; everything it changes is legible in the manifest it merges into.

clauses.subject: access-mapping
clauses.statement: An access mapping declares, per table, the column naming the governed object, the source's grain name, the projection from source principals onto `principal_kind`, the projection from source roles onto `level`, and the family.

clauses.subject: mapping-or-excluded
clauses.statement: Every table a pack lands carries an access mapping or the `excluded` declaration. There is no third state and no permissive default, so the convenient path of adding a source cannot leave a table unbound.

clauses.subject: mapping-absent
clauses.statement: A pack landing a table with neither a mapping nor an exclusion raises `VisibilityMappingAbsent` at diagnose, naming the pack and the table.

clauses.subject: mapping-asserts-nothing
clauses.statement: A mapping states how a permission model projects onto the access tables and states no audience. No field within it carries the sense of visible to the team or visible to everyone.

clauses.subject: pack-asserts-access
clauses.statement: An access-shaped key the mapping schema does not define raises `VisibilityPackAssertsAccess` by name, rather than being tolerated the way an unknown key elsewhere in a manifest is. A field nothing reads at request time can only drift from the decision the join makes.

clauses.subject: extra-fields-are-driver-inputs
clauses.statement: Fields outside the access mapping are inputs to the fetch step and reach no authorization decision.

clauses.subject: inclusion-decides-ingestion
clauses.statement: A source arriving in a reviewed diff settles what is ingested. Who reads what was ingested is settled by the credential grant, or on an organization-wide face by the join in this contract.

clauses.subject: container-allowlist
clauses.statement: Where a source exposes container membership and no permission data, the manifest carries an allowlist of container identifiers, default-deny, evaluated over each row's whole membership set.

clauses.subject: allowlist-is-all-of
clauses.statement: A row survives the allowlist when every container in its membership set is listed. An unrecognized identifier drops the row, and an empty or absent membership set drops it too.

clauses.subject: any-of-allowlist
clauses.statement: An allowlist evaluated as any-of raises `VisibilityAllowlistAnyOf` at load. Any-of admits a row also filed under a container nobody listed.

clauses.subject: no-permission-data-stays-ordinary
clauses.statement: A source returning no permission data at all takes no visibility block, stays off an organization-wide face, lands as an ordinary table whose admission is the credential grant alone, and puts no fidelity claim on the envelope.

clauses.subject: unsupported-coarse
clauses.statement: Declaring `coarse` where the source emits no container or workspace signal raises `VisibilityUnsupportedCoarse`. Where that signal is absent, the envelope has no grain to carry.

clauses.subject: defaults-are-overridable
clauses.statement: Fidelity, budget and cadence defaults in a pack are starting values an operator's manifest replaces table by table without forking the pack.

clauses.subject: decision-output
clauses.statement: Explain returns `VISIBLE` or `DENIED` together with the path producing it: the resolved principals with their link methods, asserted links marked as conferring nothing, the closure actually walked with each node's depth, the resource's observed class, every grant path found, and the watermark instant with its lag and a `CURRENT` or `STALE` verdict.

clauses.subject: row-in-a-diagnostic
clauses.statement: Returning content from the resource under explanation raises `VisibilityDiagnosticRow`. A decision endpoint cannot leak what it reasons about; an endpoint handing back unfiltered rows is a standing bypass for whoever can call it.

clauses.subject: unobserved-is-not-denied
clauses.statement: A resource with no observation on record prints `NEVER OBSERVED` rather than a denial, keeping a coverage gap distinct from a decision.

clauses.subject: denial-names-its-cause
clauses.statement: A denial standing beside a live grant path names what overrode it: a tombstone in force with its revocation instant, or an observation carrying the unknown class.

clauses.subject: unswept-source-is-stated
clauses.statement: For a source with no completed full run, the output states that reads there refuse under every declared budget, rather than reporting a per-resource decision.

clauses.subject: windowed-replay
clauses.statement: Over a window, explain evaluates the decision at every recorded observation inside it and prints each evaluation, then the coverage: observation count, run count, the widest interval between observations, and how many intervals exceeded the table's budget, each flagged.

clauses.subject: window-verdict
clauses.statement: A window verdict is `VISIBLE AT SOME OBSERVED POINT` or `NOT VISIBLE AT ANY OBSERVED POINT`, printed beneath the coverage block that qualifies it.

clauses.subject: unobserved-window
clauses.statement: A window holding no observations raises `VisibilityNoObservations` and states that no claim is available. A negative verdict over nothing observed is a claim about nothing that reads as assurance.

clauses.subject: assurance-covers-what-was-seen
clauses.statement: Between two runs a source can grant and withdraw without leaving a trace, so an assurance answer carries its observation intervals and marks each one wider than the budget.

clauses.subject: unqualified-negative
clauses.statement: An assurance answer emitted without its coverage block raises `VisibilityUnqualifiedAssurance`. A figure such as forty-one observations at a widest interval of eleven minutes against a fifteen-minute budget is weighable; a bare negative is not.

clauses.subject: groups-not-individuals
clauses.statement: A reader-facing explanation names the groups along the path and not their members. Naming who does reach a resource is a disclosure about those people.

clauses.subject: individual-named
clauses.statement: An explanation rendering member identities of a group on the path raises `VisibilityIndividualNamed`.

clauses.subject: delivered-privately
clauses.statement: An explanation reaches the person who asked for it and no audience. Stating that a named person does not reach a named resource discloses that the resource exists.

clauses.subject: audience-report
clauses.statement: Grants are rows, so the question of which resources reach more than a declared share of the organization is one aggregate over `access_grants` joined to the principal and group tables, run on the same tables the read path enforces against.

clauses.subject: report-reads-enforced-tables
clauses.statement: The report and the enforcement path consume identical rows, so a deployment measures its inherited audience without standing up a second account of it.

clauses.subject: audit-carries-visibility-fields
clauses.statement: A read against a bound table records the fidelity level, the resource grain, the lag in seconds, the degraded flag, the closure depth walked, and whether a federated leg was consulted.

clauses.subject: reporting-is-not-remediation
clauses.statement: The engine narrows a read and reports an audience; it repairs no sharing inside the source. The report hands an operator a list, and acting on that list is their access-governance work.

clauses.subject: mislabeled-table-is-an-operator-error
clauses.statement: Faithful is distinct from correct: a mirror inherits oversharing wherever manifest policy leaves it, and a sensitive table classified as record-shaped is an operator error no mechanism in this contract detects. The audience report is how it surfaces.

clauses.subject: one-enforced-view
clauses.statement: The conversational surface, the embedded tool surface, a chat-application surface and the push surface are each consumers of the same enforced view. None of them is a place where enforcement happens.

clauses.subject: surface-is-a-product-choice
clauses.statement: Choosing among those surfaces settles latency, audience and interruption, and settles no part of what a reader reaches.

clauses.subject: link-resolves-at-the-askers-scope
clauses.statement: A resource link pasted by a colleague resolves against the asker's own reachable set: one outside it is absent from the answer and disclosed as absent, rather than fetched under the poster's access.

clauses.subject: single-reader-default
clauses.statement: On a surface carrying an audience, the default reply reaches the asker alone — an ephemeral reply, a private panel, or a direct message — for every move, a question typed into a busy room included.

clauses.subject: substance-lands-durably-and-privately
clauses.statement: An ephemeral reply does not survive a reload, so an answer of any substance is delivered to a direct message or a private thread rather than left in that form.

clauses.subject: publication-is-a-deliberate-act
clauses.statement: Posting an answer where others read it is a separate act the asker takes after reading it, and not a configuration flag, a per-room default, or a mode inferred from how the question was phrased.

clauses.subject: provenance-line
clauses.statement: A posted answer carries a line stating that it was drawn from the sharer's own access and may contain material other people present do not reach.

clauses.subject: share-affordance-on-a-diagnostic
clauses.statement: A surface offering a share control on access-explanation output raises `VisibilityShareAffordance`.

clauses.subject: guarantees-end-at-publication
clauses.statement: No sweep reaches a message already posted, and the hosting platform's retention outlives every revocation the mirror records. Design at that boundary reduces harm and enforces nothing.

clauses.subject: scheduled-post-has-no-asker
clauses.statement: A scheduled or digest post originates from no reader and therefore from no reachable set. Its corpus is narrowed by manifest policy to what the destination audience reaches, read as a diff, rather than by a filter inside the posting application.

clauses.subject: askerless-audience
clauses.statement: A scheduled job posting to an audience under a service identity raises `VisibilityAskerlessAudience`, naming the destination.

clauses.subject: reader-scope-is-a-floor
clauses.statement: For an answer leaving the organization, what the reader reaches is a floor and not a ceiling: that a reader was entitled to read something settles nothing about whether a recipient outside may receive it.

clauses.subject: outbound-assembly
clauses.statement: For an outbound answer the engine assembles sourced prior answers with their provenance and hands them to a person, who makes the release decision. Policy narrows what a reader reads and does not govern what they repeat.

clauses.subject: answer-recency-is-disclosed
clauses.statement: An answer written in the present tense states when the newest row it touched landed. Freshness is bounded by pull cadence, and a status answer read off an aged pull misleads while every row inside it is real.

clauses.subject: deployment-setting
clauses.statement: Two settings derive results. Single-operator output privacy has one operator holding every contributor's rows and computing over them, where a published aggregate exposes no individual contributor. A clean room is a query pattern across a trust boundary between distinct data owners, fixed by that boundary rather than by the result being derived.

clauses.subject: mode-declaration
clauses.statement: A deployment declares its setting once at project open, and the diagnostic profile, the manifest shape and the token narrowing each follow from that declaration rather than from the presence of a derived table.

clauses.subject: single-operator-mode
clauses.statement: In the single-operator setting the write-time disclosure policy governs, a published aggregate carries cohort keys and no subject or tenant identifier column, a tenant opt-out cascades into derived tables along subject lineage, and the trail covers every read and every publication.

clauses.subject: mode-exclusion
clauses.statement: The single-operator setting carries none of the cross-owner machinery: no per-tenant signed manifest subtrees, no per-tenant signing keys, no hashed joins between tenants, no mutually-distrusting write prefixes, no escrow store. Its trust assumption is stated outright — contributors trust the operator with raw rows.

clauses.subject: disclosure-diagnostic
clauses.statement: The single-operator diagnostic validates preconditions over the project files alone: the manifest, plus the referenced statement text of each published model, read from local disk.

clauses.subject: diagnostic-request
clauses.statement: The diagnostic issues 0 requests against the object store, and a deployment validates its configuration with no network reachable.

clauses.subject: policy-coverage
clauses.statement: A published aggregate-shaped model carrying neither a disclosure policy nor a recorded opt-out fails the diagnostic with `DisclosurePolicyAbsent`.

clauses.subject: model-file
clauses.statement: A published model whose referenced statement text does not read raises `DisclosureModelUnreadable`. An unreadable file is refused rather than passed over.

clauses.subject: diagnostic-warning
clauses.statement: Two findings warn and leave the diagnostic passing: a table declaring no subject column, where the erasure cascade has nothing to follow; and a declared subject column carrying no row-level rule, where contributor rows are undivided between tokens.

clauses.subject: aggregate-shape-test
clauses.statement: The aggregate-shape test is a case-insensitive scan for a grouping clause over a model's statement text, with comments and string literals stripped ahead of the scan, and a model carries at most 1 entries declaring its output is not a cross-subject aggregate.

clauses.subject: shape-scan
clauses.statement: The declaration silences the coverage finding alone, and a disclosure policy attached to the same model still governs its build. The scan is blind in the other direction too: a global rollup, a distinct projection and a windowed partition spell no grouping clause and pass unflagged, leaving the policy on such a model for the operator to declare unprompted.

clauses.subject: clean-room
clauses.statement: A cross-owner deployment carries three deployment requirements rather than trust assumptions: per-tenant signed manifest entries, per-tenant write prefixes enforced by the object store's own access policy, and per-tenant signing keys held in each owner's own key store. A store meeting fewer than all three raises `DisclosureCleanRoomPreconditionUnmet` and the setting declines to operate against it.

clauses.subject: cross-owner-diagnostic
clauses.statement: The cross-owner profile validates the configuration ahead of any write that crosses a prefix boundary, checking the subtree signatures, the prefix policy and the key locations that the setting rests on.

clauses.subject: tenant-prefix
clauses.statement: Two or more owners' instances share one object store, each writing under its own prefix with its own write-time redaction, and each granting the other's agents tokens narrowed to hashed joins and reviewed templates.

clauses.subject: manifest-subtree
clauses.statement: Per-tenant manifest entries hang in a hash tree, and a reader verifies the path from its own subtree to the root before trusting an entry. A co-tenant rewriting the top-level manifest is detected by that verification.

clauses.subject: escrow
clauses.statement: Signing material stays in each owner's own key store and the escrow holds none of it, so a forged cross-owner grant has no signer. Per-owner encryption of the columnar files leaves the escrow operator with ciphertext.

clauses.subject: hashed-join
clauses.statement: Two owners holding disjoint datasets match on a key without either seeing the other's rows: each writer hashes the key at write time, and the join keeps the rows present on both sides.

clauses.subject: pepper
clauses.statement: A join keyed on a static pepper raises `DisclosureStaticPepper`. The floor is a per-pair pepper, re-randomized for the pairing, exchanged through escrow and rotated per join.

clauses.subject: key-domain
clauses.statement: A key space an adversary enumerates end to end is carried into the join alongside a group-size floor, and the matched rows reach a consumer as an aggregate rather than as matches.

clauses.subject: sensitive-column
clauses.statement: A column declares a `pii_type` and a masking `strategy` under `[pipeline.tables.policy.columns]`, written as `{ pii_type = "phi", strategy = "redact" }`.

clauses.subject: column-scope
clauses.statement: Classification attaches to a named column of a named table. A column carrying no declaration carries no class, and a class on a table as a whole has no meaning.

clauses.subject: pii-class
clauses.statement: The tag states which columns the operator holds to be sensitive, and the engine carries every consequence that follows — placement floors, masking, and the protections a release owes.

clauses.subject: class-vocabulary
clauses.statement: `pii_type` takes a value from the registered class set. `phi` marks protected health data; `ssn`, `phone`, `email` and `mrn` mark the identifier classes whose value space is enumerable end to end.

clauses.subject: class-vocabulary
clauses.statement: A sensitivity class outside the registered set raises `DisclosureUnknownSensitivityClass` at manifest check, and an unrecognized tag is refused rather than treated as unclassified. The column a table tags is [`10-store.md` § Reserve](./10-store.md).

clauses.subject: exhaustible-class
clauses.statement: An exhaustible class is one whose entire value space is generable offline — a social security number, a telephone number, an email address, a medical record number — where a digest is invertible by enumeration.

clauses.subject: digest
clauses.statement: A `hash` strategy standing alone over an exhaustible class raises `DisclosureDigestUnqualified`. The secondary that satisfies it is `combine = "truncate:<n>"`, the one pairing that generalizes a digest.

clauses.subject: digest-width
clauses.statement: A hash digest is 32 chars wide, and a truncation declared at or past that width removes nothing from the primary's output.

clauses.subject: token-width
clauses.statement: A token is 20 chars wide, and the same width equality holds for a truncation layered over it.

clauses.subject: combine
clauses.statement: A secondary paired over a classified column generalizes its primary's output, and a pairing that generalizes none of it raises `DisclosureCombineDoesNotGeneralize` at manifest check.

clauses.subject: truncation-width
clauses.statement: Whether a narrower truncation generalizes far enough against the column's value space rests with the operator. The engine refuses the widths that provably remove nothing and accepts the rest.

clauses.subject: combine
clauses.statement: A column's complete mask carries the primary and the secondary as one value whose halves do not separate. A consumer holding that value has no path to the primary alone, and dropping a mandated secondary is a compile error rather than a quietly weaker mask.

clauses.subject: class-reach
clauses.statement: A class declared on a column reaches every layer that touches the column — write-time removal, query-time transformation, placement resolution, and the protections a release applies to a key it joins on.

clauses.subject: privacy-unit
clauses.statement: The privacy unit is the protected entity — a tenant, or the individual a row is about — and never the row. One unit contributes many rows, and every release primitive is scoped to the unit.

clauses.subject: leak-surface
clauses.statement: A release closes two surfaces. Output leakage is the published result revealing a specific unit to a consumer holding its own rows and public side information. Process leakage is the deriving job acquiring standing raw read across every unit and becoming a centralized copy.

clauses.subject: release-pipeline
clauses.statement: A statistics release applies four steps in a fixed order: bound each unit's contribution by capping rows per unit and clamping per-row values into a declared range; suppress groups under the distinct-contributor floor; add noise calibrated to the bounded sensitivity; debit the per-unit budget.

clauses.subject: contribution-bound
clauses.statement: Contribution bounding leads the order, and the bounded sensitivity is what the noise calibration takes as input. A capped unit also enters the concentration check with a mass the cap has already limited.

clauses.subject: release-job
clauses.statement: A release executes as a journaled run-path job: it reads each unit through the replication-edge filter, applies the contribution cap at read, derives the output, and publishes it as a first-class table. The deriving principal is granted read on that output. The raw read exists for the duration of one journaled run and belongs to the engine rather than to a person as a standing capability.

clauses.subject: release-provenance
clauses.statement: Each release records which units contributed and what each was charged for a statistics release, or the pool and the resulting sizes for a segment. The record is journaled and hash-linked, and a unit audits its own inclusion and its own spend from it.

clauses.subject: central-copy
clauses.statement: Each unit keeps its own write-time redaction and its own encryption key. A deriving job reads materialized aggregates and embeddings, and no operator holds a decryptable copy of every unit's raw rows in one place.

clauses.subject: disclosure-policy
clauses.statement: A model declares the policy its materialization is safe by construction under: the permitted grouping columns, the minimum group size, the contributor key, the maximum contributor share, whether a sentinel is emitted, and the forbidden columns. A run breaching the declaration suppresses per policy or refuses, and a breaching cell is never staged.

clauses.subject: unpublished-model
clauses.statement: The declaration binds published and unpublished models alike. An unpublished cohort table read over the statement surface discloses what a published one does.

clauses.subject: contributor-breakdown
clauses.statement: A governed model's statement emits one row per group and contributor, carrying that contributor's own measures. That shape is the only one per-contributor mass reads out of, and therefore the only one a concentration ceiling is enforceable over.

clauses.subject: published-shape
clauses.statement: After suppression the engine sums each numeric measure per group and casts it back to the column's declared type. Attaching a policy moves no published column: identical statement and contract yield identical columns and an identical schema fingerprint, governed or not.

clauses.subject: grain-column
clauses.statement: A non-numeric, non-grain column rides the grouping rather than an arbitrary pick, and one that is not constant within its group raises `DisclosureDuplicateGrain`.

clauses.subject: group-key
clauses.statement: A group key that is not a subset of the permitted grouping columns raises `DisclosureGroupKeyNotPermitted`, so a finer group is unreachable by editing the statement alone.

clauses.subject: contributor-column
clauses.statement: A governed model whose statement omits the contributor key raises `DisclosureContributorKeyAbsent`. A policy that cannot count contributors has nothing to suppress on.

clauses.subject: forbidden-column
clauses.statement: A contract declaring a forbidden column, and a materialization producing one, each raise `DisclosureForbiddenColumnPublished`.

clauses.subject: key-exclusion
clauses.statement: The contributor key is a model output consumed by the policy and excluded from the published column set. Naming one column as both the contributor key and a forbidden column is coherent: the forbidden check evaluates the post-exclusion columns.

clauses.subject: policy-hash
clauses.statement: Every run records a hash over the declared policy fields, with both set-valued fields sorted ahead of hashing, so reordering a manifest entry moves no hash. The hash lands on the freshness record and on the append-only build log.

clauses.subject: policy-log
clauses.statement: The log entry outlives a build: freshness advances past a materialization and the appended entry does not, so a replay or an inspection long afterwards reads which thresholds governed a given build. A downstream attestation therefore names the exact policy behind the cells it rests on.

clauses.subject: aggregate-grant
clauses.statement: A release runs under an aggregate grant: {{authority.grant.invariant.aggregate-constraint}}

clauses.subject: grant-read
clauses.statement: Table authority for a raw read derives from read grants alone. A write-only grant and an aggregate-only grant contribute no tables to the statement surface, to search, to recall or to entity reads, and a named query grant authorizes its template's tables inside that template's session.

clauses.subject: group-ceiling
clauses.statement: An aggregate grant's groups-per-query ceiling is at least 1 entries, and a query producing more groups than the ceiling is cut at it.

clauses.subject: unit-budget
clauses.statement: A per-unit privacy budget is a catalog-tracked grant constraint of the same shape as the group-size floor: the release declares a per-run spend and a per-unit lifetime cap.

clauses.subject: budget-exhaustion
clauses.statement: The runtime debits each contributing unit at the end of a release and stops drawing on an exhausted one, raising `DisclosureUnitBudgetExhausted` where the release names that unit explicitly.

clauses.subject: segment
clauses.statement: A lookalike segment releases a segment identifier, its size, coarse composition cells, and an activation handle. Member rows and per-member scores stay inside the engine.

clauses.subject: activation-handle
clauses.statement: The action a handle names — an email, a push, an advertising-platform sync — is performed by the engine under a capability scoped to activating that segment on that channel, and never to reading its members.

clauses.subject: audience-floor
clauses.statement: A segment build declares `min_audience_size`, whose working value is 1000 subjects.

clauses.subject: audience-size
clauses.statement: A segment resolving below its declared audience floor raises `DisclosureAudienceBelowFloor` rather than emitting a sentinel, since an audience small enough to name one person is a re-identification.

clauses.subject: composition-cell
clauses.statement: A composition cell below `stats_min_cell`, whose working value is 100 subjects, collapses into a sentinel cell.

clauses.subject: member-readback
clauses.statement: Readback on a segment is `stats_only`, and a request for its members raises `DisclosureSegmentMemberReadback`.

clauses.subject: candidate-pool
clauses.statement: Posture follows where candidates come from rather than the scoring mathematics. A pool drawn from the requesting tenant's own base crosses no owner boundary. A pool the operator owns carries the size gate, activation-only output and no readback, with consent and licensing owned by the operator. A pool drawn from other tenants' end users adds per-tenant isolation and a recorded cross-party consent contract.

clauses.subject: cross-party-pool
clauses.statement: A pool spanning other tenants' end users without a recorded consent contract raises `DisclosureCrossPartyPoolUnconsented`, and the pool kind is off by default.

clauses.subject: segment-scoring
clauses.statement: A segment profile is the centroid of the seed set's embeddings. Candidates rank by approximate nearest-neighbour search over the vector index and threshold at the requested target size, with embeddings produced through the provider-agnostic model endpoint.

clauses.subject: guarantee-strength
clauses.statement: A release bounded by contribution capping, small-cell suppression and reviewed templates is described as bounded. The differential-privacy description attaches to a release that also carries noise calibrated to the bounded sensitivity and a debited per-unit budget, and a size-gated opaque segment is described as exactly that.

clauses.subject: noise-reproducibility
clauses.statement: A release carrying calibrated noise yields figures that differ between two runs over identical inputs, and a consumer comparing runs reads the difference as noise rather than as movement in the underlying data. Small cells lose usable precision under the same calibration.

clauses.subject: repeated-release
clauses.statement: Two paths lead back to a member and are named rather than implied away: fine-grained composition statistics read repeatedly across shifting parameters, where differencing isolates one member; and membership inference through activation of tiny hand-crafted segments. Coarse composition cells and rate-limited rebuilds are the standing mitigations.

clauses.subject: min-group-size
clauses.statement: A policy declares `min_group_size` as a count of distinct contributors, at least 2 subjects, and a group whose contributor count falls under it is suppressed.

clauses.subject: floor-scope
clauses.statement: The floor is a necessary guard against trivially small cells and is not itself the privacy boundary. It is silent on composition across repeated releases, presumes a fixed quasi-identifier set, leaves a homogeneous cell's shared value readable at full confidence, and says nothing about a cell one contributor dominates.

clauses.subject: contributor-share
clauses.statement: A policy declares `max_contributor_share` above 0 percent and at most 100 percent, read as a fraction of a group's metric mass.

clauses.subject: dominance
clauses.statement: A group where any single contributor's share of the sign-insensitive metric mass exceeds the ceiling is suppressed even after clearing the size floor. A group of 6 contributors where one holds 80 percent of the mass discloses that contributor's own number: the median approximates it and the sum nearly equals it.

clauses.subject: dominance-evidence
clauses.statement: A group carrying a share constraint whose per-contributor masses are unavailable at evaluation raises `DisclosureDominanceUnverifiable` and is suppressed as unverifiable rather than published.

clauses.subject: empty-policy
clauses.statement: A policy setting neither threshold raises `DisclosurePolicySuppressesNothing`, since no group under it could ever be withheld.

clauses.subject: zero-floor
clauses.statement: A `min_group_size` of zero raises `DisclosureMinGroupSizeZero`.

clauses.subject: share-range
clauses.statement: A share at or below zero, and a share above one, raise `DisclosureShareOutOfRange` as malformed.

clauses.subject: grouping-allowlist
clauses.statement: An empty list of permitted grouping columns, and a permitted name that is not column-shaped, raise `DisclosureGroupingAllowlistEmpty`.

clauses.subject: suppression-sentinel
clauses.statement: Groups withheld under either rule collapse into one field-free sentinel carried under the group key `__suppressed__`, and the sentinel names no rule.

clauses.subject: suppression-count
clauses.statement: A caller counts no withheld groups and learns no rule from the output, so neither the existence of small groups nor the presence of a dominant contributor is inferable from what comes back.

clauses.subject: suppression-tally
clauses.statement: Per-reason tallies reach the audit record and nothing else. They are absent from caller-facing rows, from the response envelope, and from the published table.

clauses.subject: sentinel-bit
clauses.statement: At build time the fact that suppression occurred rides the run's freshness record as a single boolean, surfaced when the policy asks for a sentinel, identical whether one group or a thousand were withheld.

clauses.subject: row-carriage
clauses.statement: The signal does not ride the published rows. A table with a declared column contract carries no marker in a date or integer grain column without breaking the contract check and the non-null grain invariant, and a marker row satisfying the contract is indistinguishable from data.

clauses.subject: query-template
clauses.statement: A releasing principal calls a template declared in the manifest: {{read.guard.shape.template-declaration}}

clauses.subject: template-parameter
clauses.statement: A caller submits the identifier and its arguments by name, and writes no statement text of its own.

clauses.subject: argument-binding
clauses.statement: Binding is strict: a missing argument, an unknown argument and a type-mismatched argument raise `DisclosureTemplateBindingMismatch` ahead of execution, and no argument is silently coerced.

clauses.subject: template-validation
clauses.statement: Templates validate at manifest check and again at face startup, fail-closed, before any caller reaches them.

clauses.subject: placeholder-cover
clauses.statement: Placeholders that do not cover exactly the declared parameter list raise `DisclosureTemplatePlaceholderMismatch`.

clauses.subject: statement-count
clauses.statement: A declaration holding more than one statement raises `DisclosureTemplateMultiStatement`.

clauses.subject: template-identifier
clauses.statement: A template identifier that shadows the name prefix of a built-in tool raises `DisclosureTemplateIdentifierCollision` at validation.

clauses.subject: plain-identifier
clauses.statement: A template naming anything other than a store table as a plain identifier raises `DisclosureTemplateNonPlainIdentifier` — no table functions, no bare paths, no qualified catalogs. The check is caller-independent and runs once at startup.

clauses.subject: template-enforcement
clauses.statement: A template's statement runs unrewritten while every enforcement layer still applies to what it touches: the allowlist, row restriction, column masking and placement resolution.

clauses.subject: attenuation
clauses.statement: Attenuation subsets the parent's allowlist and adds no identifier the parent withheld. The polarity is opposite to a constraint, which narrows rather than confers.

clauses.subject: template-grant
clauses.statement: Calling a template by guessed identifier raises `DisclosureTemplateNotGranted`, and listing honors the caller's grants, so an ungranted template appears nowhere.

clauses.subject: projected-tool
clauses.statement: A template reaches an agent as a tool: {{read.register.interface.template-projection}}

clauses.subject: manifest-surface
clauses.statement: The reviewed manifest is the single source of truth for the agent surface, and adding a metric is adding a template rather than deploying an application.

clauses.subject: overfetch
clauses.statement: A capped result sets the response envelope's truncation flag, established by reading exactly 1 rows past the effective ceiling rather than by shortening rows already collected.

clauses.subject: ceiling-advertisement
clauses.statement: The template's declared ceiling is advertised on the projected tool, and a consumer sizes one query against a fan-out ahead of the first call rather than discovering the bound from a shortened read.

clauses.subject: release-template
clauses.statement: A release runs a reviewed template with typed parameters. The releasing principal issues no free-form statement and no scoring pass over the unit set.

clauses.subject: governance-declaration
clauses.statement: A table's policy block declares `governance = "per-person"` or `governance = "cohort"`. A per-person table is governed at the grain of its source; a cohort table is governed by a group-size floor.

clauses.subject: default-governance
clauses.statement: A table declaring neither value resolves to cohort governance, and a read of it carries the floor.

clauses.subject: dual-governance
clauses.statement: A table declared under both regimes raises `DisclosureCohortDualGovernance`. One table is governed one way.

clauses.subject: cohort-floor
clauses.statement: On a cohort table the floor guard runs after candidate generation and before the top-K cut, so an under-floor group is dropped ahead of being counted, returned, or scored into a visible aggregate.

clauses.subject: under-floor-group
clauses.statement: An under-floor group collapses into a sentinel and its rows leave the result set, with no partial figure and no rounded stand-in in its place.

clauses.subject: cohort-widening
clauses.statement: A read recovering an under-floor group by merging it into a coarser key raises `DisclosureCohortWidening`. Widening is not a remedy for a suppressed group.

clauses.subject: per-individual-row
clauses.statement: A per-individual row from a cohort-governed deployment requires an explicit grant on the reader's token, and a read without one raises `DisclosurePerIndividualUngranted`.

clauses.subject: cohort-key
clauses.statement: A cohort table's group key names an attribute shared by many contributors — a region, an industry, a tenure band — and carries no identifier of a single person.

clauses.subject: singleton-cohort
clauses.statement: A declared cohort key whose grain resolves to one person raises `DisclosureSingletonCohort` at declaration, ahead of any row landing under it.

clauses.subject: ownership-answer
clauses.statement: An ownership question resolves to an artifact and the person attached to it — a code-owners entry, a directory's commit history, an issue's routing team, a page's owner field. The record speaks and the answer names what it says.

clauses.subject: person-artifact
clauses.statement: An ownership answer carries the artifact identifier, the field the attachment was read from, and the attached principal, so a reader checks the attachment at its source.

clauses.subject: ranked-people
clauses.statement: A ranking of people, an aggregate computed over one person, and a count of one person's activity raise `DisclosureRankedPeopleRequest`. Those shapes are measurement of a person rather than a reading of a record.

clauses.subject: span
clauses.statement: Each read emits a [[span]] carrying the full subject tuple, every field's attestation label, the token identifier with its issue time, a hash of the rewritten statement and the tables it touched, the named row rules and column masks applied, the zone counters, and the result's row count, byte count and suppressed-group count.

clauses.subject: entry
clauses.statement: An audit [[entry]] is one JSON line carrying `seq`, `prev_hash`, the attributes, and `entry_hash` computed as `sha256(seq ‖ prev_hash ‖ attributes)`.

clauses.subject: attribute-parity
clauses.statement: The attributes on an entry are the attributes on the span for that same read, plus the sequence number and the predecessor link. One read produces one of each.

clauses.subject: attribute-namespace
clauses.statement: Every attribute key is namespaced under `contextful.`, grouped by what it describes: `contextful.subject.*`, `contextful.query.*`, `contextful.row.*`, `contextful.result.*`, `contextful.erasure.*`.

clauses.subject: segment-file
clauses.statement: Entries append to a numbered segment file, one line per entry in ascending sequence, and a sibling root file closes the segment it names.

clauses.subject: hashed-statement-is-the-rewritten-one
clauses.statement: The digest covers the statement after registration and rewriting, together with the relations it resolved to, rather than the text the caller submitted.

clauses.subject: zone-counters
clauses.statement: The zone counters state how many candidates the placement filter removed and how many survived it, per read.

clauses.subject: suppression-counts
clauses.statement: Per-reason counts of suppressed groups land on the chain and reach no caller-facing row, keeping the count answerable to an auditor and closed to a consumer.

clauses.subject: genesis
clauses.statement: The [[genesis]] entry's predecessor field is the literal `sha256:` followed by 64 zeros. Removing or resequencing any entry after it breaks the linkage at that point.

clauses.subject: tip-continuity
clauses.statement: The persisted chain loads at startup and fresh entries link onto its existing tail. A segment file that is absent reads as an empty chain rather than as an error.

clauses.subject: unpersisted-entry
clauses.statement: A read whose entry cannot be written — a full disk, a denied permission, an unreachable bucket — is refused with `AuditEntryUnpersisted`, and the caller receives no rows.

clauses.subject: no-unaudited-row
clauses.statement: No path returns rows without a durable entry covering them. The refusal above is the sole outcome when the write path fails.

clauses.subject: tip-rollback
clauses.statement: A failed persist pops the in-memory tip, leaving the process state and the on-disk segment in agreement about the last accepted sequence number.

clauses.subject: query-digest
clauses.statement: The read path records `contextful.query.hash` as `sha256:<hex>` over the statement text. The statement itself, and therefore any literal inside it, stays off the chain.

clauses.subject: visibility-attributes
clauses.statement: {{visibility.explain.invariant.audit-carries-visibility-fields}}

clauses.subject: disclosure-attribute
clauses.statement: A read returning health-tagged columns records `contextful.row.phi_columns_returned`, making the count of such disclosures answerable from the record rather than reconstructed from queries.

clauses.subject: two-surfaces
clauses.statement: Two surfaces carry different jobs. [[telemetry]] is the queryable projection an operator searches; the [[chain]] is the attestable record, authoritative on whether anything was altered.

clauses.subject: projection-window
clauses.statement: The projection answers which agent read which table under which policy across a rolling window of 24 h.

clauses.subject: projection-latency
clauses.statement: Such a lookup returns within 1 s.

clauses.subject: sink-independence
clauses.statement: An unreachable telemetry sink does not stop the local chain from growing. Spans dropped at the collector leave the entries intact.

clauses.subject: default-sink
clauses.statement: The export endpoint resolves unset, and spans go to a no-op sink until an operator points them at a collector.

clauses.subject: default-egress
clauses.statement: A default configuration issues no usage ping, no license-server contact and no auto-update probe; a build that introduces an outbound call reachable without operator configuration raises `UnconfiguredEgress`.

clauses.subject: update-check
clauses.statement: An update check is opt-in through `[update] check = true`, fetches a release manifest, and transmits nothing about the deployment.

clauses.subject: verification-walk
clauses.statement: Verification walks the chain checking each entry's sequence number, its link to the predecessor, and its recomputed digest, and returns the index of the first entry that fails any of the three.

clauses.subject: verify-command
clauses.statement: `contextful audit verify` loads the persisted chain, checks every link, and exits non-zero naming the break.

clauses.subject: broken-link
clauses.statement: A recomputed digest disagreeing with the stored one, or a gap in the sequence, raises `AuditChainBroken` carrying the index of the earliest such entry.

clauses.subject: partial-history
clauses.statement: Verification over a chain whose earliest segment is absent reports the lowest sequence it holds and checks forward from there, distinguishing a truncated archive from an altered one.

clauses.subject: explanation-is-itself-recorded
clauses.statement: Running a lineage or access explanation appends its own entry, so a question asked about the record joins the record.

clauses.subject: signed-root
clauses.statement: A [[signed-root]] is `{root, count, signature}` over the tip hash of the segment it closes.

clauses.subject: appends-per-root
clauses.statement: The runtime signs a root every 16 entries.

clauses.subject: root-commit-cadence
clauses.statement: Signed roots reach the replication bucket on a configurable cadence of 10 min, carrying audit history off the node that produced it.

clauses.subject: scheme-from-the-pinned-key
clauses.statement: A root carries no algorithm field; the pinned public key's scheme decides how the signature is checked, and verification accepts a pinned key of either supported scheme.

clauses.subject: attestation
clauses.statement: A signed attestation carries `payload_hash` — the digest over the canonical payload bytes — the hex signature over that digest, and the issuer public key in its tagged distribution form.

clauses.subject: self-verifying
clauses.statement: An auditor checks the payload against its digest, then the digest against the signature and key. Both steps run without a network call and without a credential.

clauses.subject: lineage-summary
clauses.statement: `contextful audit explain --fact <id>` returns the synthesis stage, the model identity with its endpoint, the prompt digest, the contributing run, the evidence cardinality band, and the distinct source tables.

clauses.subject: cardinality-band
clauses.statement: Evidence volume appears as a [[cardinality-band]] drawn from `0`, `1-9`, `10-99`, `100+`.

clauses.subject: no-evidence-identifiers
clauses.statement: Row identifiers of contributing evidence appear nowhere in a [[lineage-attestation]]. The summary answers where a fact came from while withholding who contributed to it.

clauses.subject: policy-digest
clauses.statement: An attestation names the disclosure-policy digest its evidence tables were published under: a single value when the contributing tables agree, the full array when they differ, null when no contributing table declares one.

clauses.subject: substrate-not-attestation
clauses.statement: The engine supplies a [[compliance-substrate]] — erasure, residency-aware placement, sensitive-column tagging, a tamper-evident chain — and is not itself a certification of any regime. Mechanism sits with the engine; classification, process and audit sit with the deploying organization.

clauses.subject: at-rest-qualifier
clauses.statement: A stolen object-store credential reveals redacted columnar files for columns redacted at write time whose sidecar indexes are encrypted under the key that covers the table. That qualifier travels with the guarantee wherever it appears.

clauses.subject: query-time-mask-is-visible-at-rest
clauses.statement: A column protected at the query layer alone sits in cleartext in the bytes on disk, and a credential over the bucket reads it.

clauses.subject: qualifier-exclusions
clauses.statement: The guarantee omits three cases: a column protected at the sync layer, a vector, full-text or bloom sidecar left outside the table's encryption, and a tokenized column where the same actor holds the tokenizing key.

clauses.subject: unqualified-guarantee
clauses.statement: Authored text asserting the at-rest guarantee without the qualifier beside it raises `AtRestClaimUnqualified`.

clauses.subject: transparency-log
clauses.statement: An external append-only transparency log accepts signed roots, making a segment removed or rewritten after the fact detectable. It is off by default and no deployment depends on it.

clauses.subject: explain-command
clauses.statement: `contextful audit explain --subject <s> --resource <r>` drives the explanation from the command line and prints what it hands back. {{visibility.explain.interface.decision-output}}

clauses.subject: decision-without-a-row
clauses.statement: An access explanation returns a decision and a path. It carries no row, no field value and no excerpt from the resource it decides about.

clauses.subject: never-observed-is-not-denied
clauses.statement: A resource carrying no observation prints NEVER OBSERVED in place of a denial, and a source that has completed no full sweep prints that reads are refused under any budget.

clauses.subject: denial-names-its-cause
clauses.statement: {{visibility.explain.invariant.denial-names-its-cause}}

clauses.subject: windowed-replay
clauses.statement: Over a window, the explanation replays the decision at each recorded observation inside it and prints every one, followed by coverage: the observation count, the sweep count, the widest gap, and how many gaps exceed the budget, flagged. {{visibility.explain.shape.window-verdict}}

clauses.subject: window-without-observations
clauses.statement: A window holding zero observations returns `AssuranceWindowEmpty` and the words "no claim can be made" in place of a negative verdict.

clauses.subject: assurance-is-scoped
clauses.statement: [[negative-assurance]] covers observed states. Output carries the observation intervals and flags every gap wider than the budget, and a bare "never" without that qualification is refused.

clauses.subject: groups-not-individuals
clauses.statement: {{visibility.explain.invariant.groups-not-individuals}}

clauses.subject: overshare-report
clauses.statement: Grants are rows, so the [[overshare-report]] is a single aggregate over the mirror answering which resources a share of the organization above a declared threshold can read. It runs over the same tables the read path enforces on.

clauses.subject: overshare-threshold
clauses.statement: The organizational share above which a resource appears in the report is a parameter of the query, and the report prints the threshold it ran under beside the rows it returns.

clauses.subject: reporting-is-not-remediation
clauses.statement: The engine narrows and reports; repairing a source's sharing stays with the operator's access-governance work.

clauses.subject: subject-column
clauses.statement: A table names its subject-identifier column in the manifest, as `subject_id = "user_id"` under `[[pipeline.tables]]`. Erasure addresses a person through that column.

clauses.subject: undeclared-subject-column
clauses.statement: A subject erasure against a table that declares no subject column raises `ErasureSubjectUndeclared` naming the table, rather than guessing at a key.

clauses.subject: ledger
clauses.statement: The catalog table `forget_requests(request_id, tenant_hash, subject_hash, requested_at, completed_at)` holds one row per erasure request.

clauses.subject: hashed-ledger-keys
clauses.statement: `tenant_hash` and `subject_hash` are written `sha256:<hex>`, one of the pair null per path, and the ledger holds no cleartext identifier at any position.

clauses.subject: ledger-row-brackets-the-work
clauses.statement: A ledger row opens ahead of the first tombstone and takes its `completed_at` after the last commit, so an interrupted operation leaves an open row naming what was in flight.

clauses.subject: key-hashed-at-the-boundary
clauses.statement: The verb accepts a cleartext subject or tenant key, hashes it at the command boundary, and writes nothing but the digest onward.

clauses.subject: ledger-survives-a-rebuild
clauses.statement: `forget_requests` counts as engine journal state rather than derivable cache, and sits outside the set a catalog rebuild drops. A rebuilt catalog still carries every completed request.

clauses.subject: forget-command
clauses.statement: `contextful context forget` is the single audited verb: `--subject <key>` drives the subject path, `--tenant <id>` the purge, `--no-cascade` narrows the subject path to direct rows, `--fail-closed` arms the restaging gate, `--clear-stale` releases it.

clauses.subject: direct-tombstones
clauses.statement: The subject path writes a [[tombstone]] over every row about that person in the subject-keyed shapes: facts keyed on `subject_id`, entities keyed on `entity_id`, preferences keyed on `subject_id`.

clauses.subject: lineage-cascade
clauses.statement: A derived fact whose provenance lists evidence referencing the subject key, or referencing any identifier the direct pass tombstoned, is invalidated in the same operation. The [[cascade]] travels one lineage hop.

clauses.subject: cascade-reaches-everything-derived
clauses.statement: One hop covers every artifact the store derived about the subject, including rows a self-directed run filed of its own accord.

clauses.subject: no-cascade-flag
clauses.statement: `--no-cascade` confines the operation to direct rows and records that narrowing on the chain, leaving an incomplete erasure visible to the next auditor.

clauses.subject: markers-precede-the-return
clauses.statement: With replication configured, both paths commit their tombstones and cascade markers as part of the operation itself rather than deferring them to a later push. The verb returns after that commit.

clauses.subject: failed-push-degrades
clauses.statement: A push that fails downgrades to a warning. The markers hold on local disk and reconcile at the next successful commit.

clauses.subject: staleness-marker
clauses.statement: `--fail-closed` writes a `{subject_hash, executed_at}` object at the store root once the cascade completes.

clauses.subject: stale-derived-read
clauses.statement: While that object stands, every fact read — recall, command line and tool surface alike — is refused with `ErasureRestagingRequired`, which names the re-synthesis the operator owes and the verb that clears it.

clauses.subject: gate-clears-on-attestation
clauses.statement: `--clear-stale` removes the object after synthesis has run over the post-erasure store, and the operator's attestation is what the removal records.

clauses.subject: marker-replicates-as-bookkeeping
clauses.statement: The [[staleness-marker]] holds no rows and belongs to the set of root objects a replica receives while a table is withheld, so a replica inherits the gate in place of serving derived facts built before the erasure.

clauses.subject: tenant-rewrite
clauses.statement: No partition segment separates tenants on disk, so a [[purge]] is a columnar rewrite: every file the read path can reach — committed runs, compaction snapshots, each model build — is rewritten retaining the rows outside the named tenant.

clauses.subject: purge-order
clauses.statement: A purge sweeps a fixed order — committed run files, then compaction snapshots, then each model build, then the memory mirror — and records a per-stage count as it goes.

clauses.subject: memory-mirror-uses-the-same-predicate
clauses.statement: The memory mirror is rewritten under the predicate the columnar files were rewritten under, leaving no derived copy admitting rows the base tables dropped.

clauses.subject: purge-predicate
clauses.statement: The rewrite keeps `NOT COALESCE(CAST(<tenant_col> AS VARCHAR) = '<tenant>', FALSE)`, byte for byte the complement of the filter a tenant-scoped grant compiles. The coalesce retains a null-tenant row that a bare inequality drops.

clauses.subject: non-string-tenant-column
clauses.statement: A tenant column of a non-string type raises `PurgeTenantColumnType` in place of an implicit cast, since a guessed cast direction is where the rewrite and the read filter part company.

clauses.subject: undeclared-tenant-column
clauses.statement: The purge resolves where a tenant lives from the model's outermost partition key; no model declaring one raises `PurgeTenantUndeclared`.

clauses.subject: holds-yield-to-erasure
clauses.statement: Garbage collection skips a held build; erasure does not. A held materialization carrying the tenant's rows is rewritten like any other file and stays pinnable afterwards.

clauses.subject: write-lock-serializes-the-sweep
clauses.statement: The rewrite holds the per-model write lock across a table's whole sweep — the same lock builds, holds and collection take — leaving no window for a concurrent build to publish a fresh materialization behind it.

clauses.subject: capability-token-caller
clauses.statement: A purge presented with a capability token is refused with `PurgeRequiresOwner`, and that refusal is evaluated ahead of anything that tells the caller what the store contains.

clauses.subject: chain-attributes
clauses.statement: Each erasure appends to the same chain the read path writes, carrying `contextful.erasure.subject_hash` or `contextful.erasure.tenant_hash`, the request identifier, the stated reason, and the direct and cascaded counts.

clauses.subject: chain-does-not-redisclose
clauses.statement: Those attributes are hashes, so the chain confirms an erasure reached every derived artifact while naming nobody.

clauses.subject: replica-holds-until-refresh
clauses.statement: A replica consumes materialized snapshots read-only and holds erased rows until its next refresh brings the rewritten files.

clauses.subject: propagation
clauses.statement: Request to last-replica refresh completes within 72 h.

clauses.subject: expedited-collection
clauses.statement: Snapshots superseded by an erasure collect on an expedited schedule of 24 h.

clauses.subject: default-retention
clauses.statement: Snapshots superseded by ordinary writes collect against a retention default of 7 d.

clauses.subject: body
clauses.statement: A [[receipt]] carries `receipt_version`, a `receipt-coverage` block, `tenant_hash`, an engine-minted `request_id` prefixed `prg_`, `completed_at`, per-table rows removed and files rewritten with the build identifiers touched, the derived-table cascade, and `prior_request_id`.

clauses.subject: signature-block
clauses.statement: The signature block is `{payload_hash, signature, public_key}` over the canonical payload, computed under Ed25519 or ES256 as the pinned key's scheme dictates.

clauses.subject: canonical-payload
clauses.statement: The payload is canonicalized before hashing, and `payload_hash` names the digest of exactly those bytes. A verifier re-canonicalizes and recomputes rather than trusting the transmitted digest.

clauses.subject: claim-is-rewrite-and-exclude
clauses.statement: Version 1 attests rewrite-and-exclude across the canonical store: run files, snapshots, model builds, and the memory mirror.

clauses.subject: coverage-names-exclusions
clauses.statement: The `receipt-coverage` block names what falls outside the claim — the replication bucket, replicas, and physical destruction of media — in the artifact itself rather than in surrounding prose.
